Vietnam Full Tour Plan
Vietnam Itinerary 8/10/12 Days
Vietnam Trip from India
#vietnamtravel  #vietnamtrip  #vietnamitinerary  #travelguide   #vietnamtourism  #asiatravel  #halongbaytour  #hoian  #phuquoc 

Planning a Vietnam trip from India? 🇻🇳 This video is your complete Vietnam Travel Guide 2025 – covering North, Central, and South Vietnam with the best time to visit, visa details, flights, itinerary options, transport, and stay tips.

✨ In this video, you’ll get:

The best time to visit Vietnam 🌤️

Easy e-Visa process & flights from India ✈️

12-Day Vietnam Itinerary (customised for 8 & 10 days) covering Hanoi, Halong Bay, Ninh Binh, Hoi An, Da Nang, Ho Chi Minh City, Mekong Delta & Phu Quoc 🌴

Accommodation recommendations – from budget to luxury 🏨

Transport tips for families, honeymooners, and solo travellers 🚖

📍 Highlights include: Halong Bay Cruise, Ba Na Hills & Golden Bridge, Hoi An Lantern Town, Cu Chi Tunnels, Mekong Delta, and Phu Quoc Island beaches.

👉 Whether you’re planning a family holiday, honeymoon, or adventure trip, this guide will help you plan the perfect Vietnam itinerary from India.

👍 Don’t forget to Like, Share & Subscribe for more travel guides across Asia!

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

💰 Approximate Vietnam Trip Budget (12 Days from India, per person)
1. ✈️ Flights (India ↔ Vietnam + Domestic Flights)

International Flights (India ↔ Hanoi / Ho Chi Minh): ₹20,000 – ₹28,000 (round trip, economy, if booked in advance).

Domestic Flights (Hanoi → Da Nang, Da Nang → Ho Chi Minh, Ho Chi Minh → Phu Quoc, Phu Quoc → Ho Chi Minh): ₹12,000 – ₹16,000.
➡️ Total Flights: ₹32,000 – ₹44,000

2. 🏨 Accommodation (per night)

Budget hotels/hostels: ₹1,200 – ₹2,000

Mid-range 3★–4★ hotels: ₹3,000 – ₹5,000

Luxury resorts: ₹7,000 – ₹12,000
➡️ For mid-range stays (11 nights): ₹35,000 – ₹50,000

3. 🍜 Food & Drinks

Street food meals: ₹200 – ₹400

Restaurant meals: ₹500 – ₹1,000
➡️ Average per day: ₹1,000 – ₹1,500
➡️ Total (12 days): ₹12,000 – ₹18,000

4. 🚖 Local Transport & Transfers

Grab (ride-hailing app), taxis, buses, short tours: ₹600 – ₹1,000/day
➡️ Total (12 days): ₹7,000 – ₹12,000

5. 🎟️ Sightseeing, Tours & Activities

Halong Bay Cruise (overnight/day): ₹4,000 – ₹8,000

Ba Na Hills & Golden Bridge: ₹2,000 – ₹3,000

Mekong Delta tour: ₹2,500 – ₹3,500

Phu Quoc island hopping: ₹3,000 – ₹4,000

Other entry tickets, shows, local tours: ₹5,000 – ₹8,000
➡️ Total Activities: ₹16,000 – ₹25,000

6. 📄 Visa & Miscellaneous

Vietnam e-Visa: $25 (~₹2,100)

SIM card, tips, souvenirs, shopping: ₹5,000 – ₹8,000

✅ Estimated Total Budget (per person)

Budget Travel: ₹85,000 – ₹1,00,000

Mid-Range Travel (comfortable hotels + tours): ₹1,15,000 – ₹1,35,000

Luxury Travel (resorts, premium cruises, private tours): ₹1,60,000+

👉 Tip: If you shorten to 8–10 days (skipping Phu Quoc), you can save around ₹20,000 – ₹25,000 per person.

transcript: If you are planning a Vietnam tour from India, stop right here. You have clicked on the perfect video. In the next few minutes, I will give you a complete Vietnam tour plan covering North, Central, and South Vietnam. You will learn about the best time to visit, visa process, flights, family, and honeymoon itineraries along with transport and accommodation tips. But here's the big question. What's the ideal number of days to explore Vietnam without missing on its best experiences? Is it 8, 10, or 12 days? Well, before we get into that, let's first understand Vietnam better. Vietnam located in Southeast Asia is divided into three main regions. Hanoi, Halong Bay, and Ninbin with stunning landscapes and cultural heritage forming the northern side of the country. While Daang Hoyan famous for beaches, lantern towns and imperial history is in central Vietnam. Ho Chi Min City, Meong Delta and Fukquok Island known for modern lifestyles, floating markets and island resorts forming the country's southern part. Now that you know the three main regions of Vietnam, the question is which season is best to cover all of them comfortably? The best time to visit Vietnam is during October to April when the weather is pleasant across most regions. Summer May to August can be hot and humid but is good for beach lovers while the monsoon season that is September brings heavy rain in some areas. But what's the smartest way to divide your days across these regions? Whether you are planning for an 8 day, 10day, or 12-day tour to Vietnam, here is an itinerary for each duration. Let's begin with the 12-day tour plan. And then I will customize it for 8 and 10 days. But please remember, the more days you have, the more comfortably you can explore all the parts of this beautiful country. Day one. On the first day of our Vietnam tour, we landed in Hanoi, the famous city in the north. You will easily get direct flights from all major Indian cities to Vietnam. And that made our journey smooth, taking around 5 hours. The e visa process was easy and we cleared immigration quickly. After a short rest at the hotel, we began exploring Hanoi's old quarter in the evening. The narrow streets were full of shops, cafes, and street vendors selling everything from shuvenas to sizzling Vietnamese snacks. We also walked around 1 p.m. Lake, a peaceful spot in the middle of the city. As the sun set, we enjoyed the famous water puppet show, a traditional performance that we all enjoyed. Day two, our second day was reserved for exploring Hanoi's history. We started with the Ho Chi Min Mosolum where we learned about the country's most respected leader. Next, we visited the OnePillar Pagota followed by the Temple of Literature, which was Vietnam's first university built in, 2017. Later in the afternoon, we headed to Trunkwalk Pagoda, the oldest Buddhist temple in Hanoi, standing beautifully by the lake. In the evening, we strolled through the night market, testing local street food and shopping for handmade crops. Day three. On the third day, we went to Ninb, often called Halong Bay on land. We took a small boat through Tamco Cake surrounded by rice fields and limestone mountains. [Music] Then we climbed the Mua Cave viewpoint which gave us a panoramic view. [Music] Day four. On the fourth day, we set out for Halong Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage site around 3 hours from Hanoi. Boarding our cruise ship, we sailed among thousands of limestone islands rising from emerald waters. We explored hidden caves, went kayaking, enjoyed fresh seafood lunch on the deck. The beauty of the bay felt like something out of a painting. It was one of the most memorable days of our trip. Day five. On the fifth morning, we flew to Dhanang, located in central Vietnam. From there, a short drive took us to Hoan, a charming ancient town. We checked into a cozy riverside hotel and then explored the lantern lit streets in the evening. Goan felt magical with colorful lanterns hangering across the streets, tailor shops, and little cafes along the river. We also took a short boat ride where we released paper lanterns into the water making wishes. Day six. The sixth day was dedicated to Bana Hills, a fantasy theme park in the mountains. A thrilling cable car ride took us up offering stunning views. The highlight was the golden bridge held up by two giant stone hands, a mustsee for everyone. We also visited the flower gardens, French village, and fun indoor games at Fantasy Park. By evening, we returned to Hoyan to relax by the river. Day seven. On the seventh day, we flew south to Ho Chi Min City, Vietnam's largest city. Our first stop was the Coochie Tunnels, an underground network used during Vietnam War. Crawling through the narrow tunnels was adventurous, but best suited for adults and older kids. Later we explored Benthan market full of shuveners, handiccrafts and local snacks. Day eight. The eighth day was reserved for the Meong Delta. We drove a couple of hours out of the city and boarded a wooden boat. Floating past coconut plantations, fruit orchards, and small villages gave us a glimpse of rural Vietnam. By evening, we returned to Ho Chi Min City. In the evening, we boarded a Saigon River dinner cruise, enjoying the skyline lit up with skyscrapers and colonial buildings. Day nine. On the ninth day, we flew to Folk Island, Vietnam's tropical paradise. After checking into our beachfront resort, we relaxed at Long Beach, famous for its golden sands and stunning sunset. Day 10. The 10th day was dedicated to exploring the island's attractions. We started with the Fukquok cable car, one of the longest oversea cable cars in the world, which took us to Hon Island for water activities. [Music] In the afternoon, we visited Sao Beach, one of the most beautiful beaches in Vietnam with powdery white sand and turquoise water. Later, we spent the evening at Grand World Fukwalk, a massive entertainment complex with colorful Venice style canels, light shows, shopping, and lively performances. Day 11. On our final day, we went on an island hopping tour by speedboat. We visited smaller islands around Fukquok such as Gangghi Island for snorkeling, Mirat Island for swimming, and coral reefs filled with tropical fish. It was a day full of sea, sun, and adventure. By late afternoon, we returned to our resort. Day 12. On the 12th day, we headed to the airport for our flight back to Ho Chi Min City connecting onward to India. Now, if you have 8 days in hand, you can skip Fukquak Island and Ninbin day trip from this itinerary for a 10-day tour. Skip only Fukquok Island, while the rest of the tour remains the same as Zav. But once you have decided your itinerary, the next question is where should you stay for the best experience. [Music] Vietnam offers a wide range of stays from luxury resorts, boutique hotels to budget hotels. In Hanoi and Ho Chi Min City, stay in the old quarter or near district one for easy access. In Hoya, stay near the ancient town for a romantic vibe. In Dhanang or Fukwok, beach resorts are best for families and honeymooners. For online booking links, please check the description box below. Now you know where to stay in each city depending on your style and budget. But how do you actually move around Vietnam efficiently? Vietnam has convenient domestic flights between Hanoi, Daang and Ho Chi Min City. For local travel, taxis and private cars can be hired for sightseeing. Trains and buses are budget options, but families prefer flights for comfort. Hope you got all the information you need to plan your Vietnam trip. If you love this tour plan, don't forget to like and share the video. And here is my question for you. If you had to pick only one, would you choose the mountains of Halong Bay or the beaches of Fukquok? Tell me in the comments below. Thanks for watching it.

From the bustling streets of Hanoi to the breathtaking landscapes of Ninh Binh, the iconic Ha Long Bay, the stunning rice terraces of Sapa, and the unforgettable Ha Giang Loop, this guide covers the best experiences North Vietnam has to offer.

Whether you're traveling on a budget, with family, as a couple, or solo, this video will help you plan the perfect North Vietnam itinerary while avoiding common travel mistakes.

meta.title: 2025 BEST HOI AN STREET FOOD Tour 🇻🇳 Eating Like A Local In Vietnam
meta.description:
Food we have NEVER heard of or tried BEFORE 🍜 on the Ultimate HOI AN STREET FOOD Tour in Vietnam

Join us as we dive into the vibrant streets of Hoi An, Vietnam, for the ultimate street food adventure! Guided by the legendary Sam, we explored the best local dishes, iconic markets, and hidden gems. This tour was an unforgettable culinary journey—packed with bold flavors, rich traditions, and insider tips to help you eat like a local. 🌟

📍 What We Ate in This Video:

1️⃣ Bún Chả Ta (Noodle Soup): A flavorful broth with fresh herbs and noodles. Hoi An Ancient Town 🍲
2️⃣ Cà Phê Trứng (Egg Coffee): Creamy, sweet, and the perfect pick-me-up. Hoi An Ancient Town ☕
3️⃣ Bánh Xèo (Rice Pancake): Crispy, savory, and stuffed with goodness. 📍 Hoi An Center Market 🥞
4️⃣ Xí Mà (Black Sesame Soup): A unique dessert that’s rich and nutty. 
5️⃣ Cơm Gà (Chicken Rice): A Hoi An classic that’s comforting and flavorful. Hoi An Ancient Town 🍗🍚
6️⃣ Bánh Mì: Vietnam’s most famous sandwich—crispy bread, fresh fillings, and bold flavors. 📍 115 Trần Cao Vân Street, Hoi An, Quảng Nam 🥖
7️⃣ Cao Lầu (Noodles): A regional specialty with thick noodles and pork. 📍 28 Thái Phiên, Hoi An Ancient Town 🍜
8️⃣ Bánh Bèo (Steamed Rice Cake): Soft, savory cakes topped with crispy goodness. 📍 Trần Cao Vân Street 🍘
9️⃣ Sinh Tố (Mixed Fruit Smoothie): Refreshing, fruity, and the perfect way to cool down. 📍 110 Nguyễn Trường Tộ, Hoi An Ancient Town 🥤

🛵 Tour Details:
We booked our tour through Hanoi Street Food Tour http://www.hanoistreetfoodtour.com/ and were guided by Sam, who made the experience unforgettable with his local knowledge and warm personality. Highly recommend this tour for anyone visiting Hoi An! 🙌

That "leave the shoes for the sandal" process for the bathroom wasn't around when I was living and working in VN but it makes sense.  Those sandals are in that area and are not walked on the gravel so they're cleaner than your shoes.  Vietnamese people leave shoes and sandals at the door and walk barefoot in the house which I agree as much cleaner than us American wearing shoes in our home.  I think it's filthy how we wear our shoes in the house, put them on our couch, etc.

As for the caves, those are beautiful and really look surreal with the external sunlight beaming inside.

meta.title: VIETNAM under Rs.65000 for 2 PEOPLE | BUDGET breakdown | HANOI & SAPA | Complete guide 🇻🇳
meta.description:
Can you really travel to Vietnam for under ₹65,000 as a couple? 🇻🇳✨

In this video, we're sharing exactly how we planned and completed our 7 Days / 6 Nights Vietnam trip covering Hanoi and Sapa for under ₹65,000 for two people.

From flights, hotels, transportation, food, activities, shopping, and every major expense in between, we've broken down our complete budget so you can plan your own Vietnam trip with confidence.

Our itinerary:
📍 Hanoi (2 Days)
📍 Sapa (3 Days, 2 Nights)
📍 Hanoi (1.5 Days & 1 Night)

In this vlog, you'll find:
💰 Complete trip cost breakdown
✈️ Flight expenses and booking tips
🏨 Hotel recommendations
🚌 Hanoi to Sapa transportation details
🍜 Food and café recommendations
📸 Must visit attractions and experiences
🎒 Travel tips and things we learned along the way
🇻🇳 Honest insights on what is worth your money and what isn't

Whether you're planning your first international trip, looking for a budget friendly destination, or dreaming about visiting Vietnam, this video will help you understand the real costs of traveling through Hanoi and Sapa.

If you have any questions about Vietnam travel, leave them in the comments and we'll be happy to help.

📸 Follow our travel adventures: @dustysuitcases

#Vietnam #VietnamTravel #Hanoi #Sapa #VietnamBudgetTrip #VietnamTravelGuide #BudgetTravel #InternationalTravel #TravelVlog #DustySuitcases

meta.title: Ba Na Hills Complete Travel Guide 2026 | Golden Bridge, Tickets, Rides & Tips
meta.description:
Planning a visit to Ba Na Hills from Da Nang? This complete Ba Na Hills travel guide covers everything you need to know before visiting Sun World Ba Na Hills in Vietnam.

We visited Ba Na Hills at the end of May and explored the Golden Bridge, French Village, Moon Kingdom, Fantasy Park, Lunar Castle, gardens, temples, live shows and the Alpine Coaster.
In this video, we cover:

• How to reach Ba Na Hills from Da Nang
• Distance and travel time from Da Nang city
• Why you should book a cab in advance
• Best time to reach and avoid crowds
• Ba Na Hills ticket prices in INR and USD
• Booking tickets through Klook
• What to carry for unpredictable mountain weather
• Golden Bridge and Le Jardin D’Amour
• Moon Kingdom and Lunar Castle
• French Village and Sun Kingdom
• Fantasy Park rides and indoor attractions
• Alpine Coaster price and experience
• Live shows and performances
• Food and restaurant options
• Whether staying at Mercure Ba Na Hills is worth it
• The best route to cover Ba Na Hills in one day

Ba Na Hills is located around 25 to 30 kilometres from central Da Nang and is one of the most popular day trips in Vietnam. Reaching early, wearing comfortable shoes and carrying a rain cover can make your experience considerably better.

Our Klook booking for three adults cost ₹9,037.92, which was approximately ₹3,013 per person. Prices may vary depending on the date, package and exchange rate.

Watch the complete video before planning your Ba Na Hills trip.

#BaNaHills #DaNang #VietnamTravel #GoldenBridge #SunWorldBaNaHills

meta.title: My Son Sanctuary Vietnam - Amazing Champa Temples near Hoi An | Day Trip Vlog
meta.description:
Join us on a day trip from Hoi An to the ancient My Son Sanctuary, a UNESCO World Heritage site nestled in the lush jungles of Vietnam. In this vlog, we explore the stunning red-brick temples that once served as the religious heart of the Champa Kingdom. Dating back to the 4th century, My Son is an architectural marvel dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva. We’ll dive into its fascinating history, admire the intricate carvings, and learn how this ancient site survived the test of time. This place reminded us a lot of Angkor Wat in Cambodia even though WAY smaller in size.
Whether you’re a history buff or just love exploring beautiful, hidden gems, My Son is a must-see destination. Wonder if My Son Sanctuary is worth visiting? Then keep watching! Don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more travel adventures!

meta.title: Marble Mountain, Da Nang: 10 Things Most Tourists Don't Know
meta.description:
Planning to visit Marble Mountain in Da Nang, Vietnam? Before you go, here are 10 things most tourists don't know - from the best time to see Huyen Khong Cave to hidden caves, crowded hours, climbing conditions, and the routes that can completely change your visit.
Most visitors spend around two hours at Marble Mountain and leave thinking they've seen everything. But after returning four different times, I realized how easy it is to miss some of the most memorable parts of this remarkable place.
In this video, I'll share what first-time visitors should know before visiting Marble Mountain, including when to arrive, what to expect from the climb, how much time to allow, which caves to prioritize, and why Am Phu Cave shouldn't be missed.
If you're planning your first trip to Da Nang and Hoi An, this guide will help you experience Marble Mountain with better timing, better expectations, and fewer surprises.
Next, I'll show you how to plan your first Da Nang and Hoi An trip before you book anything.

comments.author: @itsvirtualvisa
comments.text:
Hi…by using your tourist visa yes, you can search for a job, but you CANNOT legally work on a Tourist Visa. 

If you enter on a Tourist Visa to search for jobs locally:
1. Attend interviews and sign the employment agreement in Vietnam.
2. Employer processes your Work Permit documents locally.  
3. Do a quick "Visa Run" (fly/bus to neighboring Cambodia, Thailand, or Laos) to switch from Tourist Visa to your new Work Visa, then re-enter Vietnam.

If you’re planning a trip and wondering:

Is Da Nang worth visiting in January?

comments.author: @D4FChennel
comments.text:
I’ve been spending a lot of time in Vietnam, and honestly, this video doesn’t really match my experience.

Of course scams exist — just like anywhere. I’ve taken taxis, bought things at markets and shops, and sometimes noticed different prices. But I usually check a few places first, get an idea of the normal price, and then decide. Once you know roughly what something should cost, it’s not difficult to avoid being overcharged.

For me, Vietnam feels like a very safe place overall. I’ve spent a lot of time here and have had overwhelmingly normal, friendly interactions with people.

I think there’s a big difference between saying “scams happen in Vietnam” and making it sound like Vietnam is full of scammers. The first is true; the second doesn’t match my experience at all.

comments.author: @ArneRolfsson
comments.text: I just remembered a funny thing that happened to me in Nha Trang. If you've been in Vietnam for a while you've probably encountered the odd motorcycle driver approaching you, asking: How long have you been in Vietnam? If you say anything less than 1-3 months he would try to sell you a guided tour package of his own. But whenever I said I've been here 6 month or more, they just said oh, and drove away. So my advice is never let anyone who approach you know that you're a newbie!

comments.author: @ArneRolfsson
comments.text:
There's so many different scams, here as in many other countries. Personally I've had a very "friendly" Grab driver who in the end planned to dump me in a crocodile farm after robbing me. Buying cigarettes by street vendors around 75% more expensive. Scales at local markets 
weighing 10-15% wrong. Oranges injected with sugar solution. The shoe shine guys, another Grab driver trying to snatch my phone. An old woman trying to sell a banana pancake for 100.000 dong. And so on. It's a never ending story. Yet I've been living here for almost 6 years now and wouldn't want to be anywhere else. Because most people are really friendly and curious and want to interact. Crimes of course do happen but they are solved in a rapid pace. And obviously not all taxi drivers are scammers. I once dropped my phone, essential for me to survive, in a taxi in HCMC. After 10 minutes he returned where he dropped me off with my phone and completely refused the money I wanted to give him.

comments.text:
Scam 5 is pretty common. I visited Vietnam recently and both in Hanoi and Saigon they tried this on me. I let it go because it was not a significant amount, but going forward I will simply ignore the aunties. 

1) Aunty walked towards me and offered me a free pastry ball (tasted actually pretty good, it was dry and old, but it was good). I asked how much. She said 30k, so I said yes, gave her 200k and she did not return enough change and said (after I asked) the price was 80k for 5 of the pastry balls, which obviously is overpriced. Clearly, she lied. As it turned out, she only returned 110k effectively charging 90k. In any case, I let it go. It was my first evening in Hanoi and I did not want to get upset.

2) Bought some fruit and similarly to 1) after I paid 100k for fruit that was supposed to cost 85k, I only received 5k with the aunty then saying the total was 95k. Again, too small of an amount to bother. The fruit was actually pretty good (in particular the bananas). 

In any case, I will have pen and paper with me and will be exceedingly careful if at all I ever buy from street aunties in Vietnam. And I will carry small denomination bills so that I can pay exactly what was agreed upon after taking possession of the products first. But, to be honest, to the most part I will not bother and ignore those cute aunties. Love Vietnam, but this reflects poorly on the country.

Vietnam in winter is very cold in the north, it gets warmer as you go south. But Hanoi is very cold, don't come in the winter expecting tropical temperatures.

Danang is warmer but still not very hot in winter.

Stick to Nha Trang and further south if you want really tropical weather in the winter.

meta.title: Vietnam Street Food - ULTIMATE PHO TOUR!! (How Pho Became World’s #1 Vietnamese Food)
meta.description:
🍜 Bangkok Chinatown - 5 Best Foods: https://youtu.be/WRLVrfIBS1k
👕 T-shirts: https://store.migrationology.com/ 

HANOI, VIETNAM: Welcome to Hanoi, Vietnam, the capital of the most well known Vietnamese food around the world - pho! Today I’m hanging out with my friend Khoa from @Hanoifood and we’re taking you on an unforgettable pho tour of Hanoi. We’ll be eating at 5 of the best pho restaurants and stalls in Hanoi, and sharing with you the history of how pho came about and how it took over the world as the most famous of all Vietnamese food.

Huge thanks to Khoa: @Hanoifood 

Here are all the pho spots we ate at in this video:

1. Phở Mạnh Cường (https://goo.gl/maps/MLh55yK9cy1x2gaKA) 
Price: 55,000 VND ($2.31) per bowl
We’re starting off with a simple bowl of pho, but very popular for breakfast in Hanoi.

2. Pho Thin (https://goo.gl/maps/LM5viiFn85xSBhcNA) 
Price: 70,000 VND ($2.94) per bowl 
This is one of the most famous bowls of pho in Hanoi, and they even have restaurants abroad. One of their signatures is that they stir fry the beef instead of boiling it. It’s not doubt one of the best bowls of pho you’ll ever eat.

3. Phở Bò Ấu Triệu (https://goo.gl/maps/iGbqejrNy3dAnYsA8) 
Price: 60,000 VND ($2.52) per bowl 
Another bowl of extraordinary beef pho, this was one of my favorites of the day.

4. Phở gà Phương (https://goo.gl/maps/Wckk9d85ZHRUna7X8) 
Price: 100,000 VND ($4.20) for full toppings 
Along with beef, chicken pho has a unique history and Khoa takes me to one of his favorite places - this place is outstanding!

5. Phở Hạnh (https://goo.gl/maps/ukmNLSRyY5gGAnpm9) 
Price: 50,000 VND ($2.10) per bowl, 80,000 VND (3.36) salad 
To wrap up this ultimate Vietnamese street food pho tour we tried one more bowl of chicken pho - but this time a dry version with soup on the side. Additionally the cabbage chicken salad was life-changing.

Thank you for watching this ultimate Vietnamese street food tour in Hanoi!

I watched a video episode where Mark and his Vietnamese friend visited famous pho restaurants in Hanoi. I was filled with emotions and amazed when I switched to his channel to watch how he talked about Hanoi Pho. As a Hanoi local and a passionate lover of traditional Hanoi cuisine, I truly admire his communication style.
1- The way he filmed and narrated was very engaging, energetic, and incredibly natural.
2- He did research on the origins of Pho, so the video editing truly became high-quality, providing useful information to the viewers. He was clever in respecting his Vietnamese friend.
3- Most importantly, what I highly appreciate is that even though he is not Vietnamese, he had a certain knowledge about Pho before tasting it. His eating style and approach were quite close to the criteria of enjoying Pho. I can assert that with his extensive experience and vast knowledge of cuisine, he had found the most proper way to eat Pho for himself. However, for the audience, he went through the additional experience of tasting various flavor profiles and exploring different notes to convey to his viewers.
4- I hope that the next time he visits Hanoi, he can find a local guide who can help him discover more mysterious Pho places. A guide who possesses more knowledge about the culinary history and food culture, enabling them to interact directly with him on the set. That would be truly priceless.
I truly admire and love him.

comments.text:
There are two major beef Pho styles in Vietnam
Northern style (think Ha Noi):
+ The original style. But can mostly be found only within Vietnam, quite rare in the South and even rarer oversea
+ The broth is much clearer and a bit mild compare to Southern style. Making the broth clear requires some serious techniques!
+ Thinner noodle
+ More spring onion. Less brown/white onion
+ Dough stick (youtiao) is a standard side dish. NO vegetable & herb side dish
+ Table condiments: pickle garlic, chili paste (very finely grounded chili in vinegar, mostly homemade) & fresh chili. NO hoisin.

Southern style (think Sai Gon (or Ho Chi Minh city)): 
+ The most popular style outside of Vietnam. The majority of Pho in the US & Australia are Southern style. I find Australian version of Pho is much closer to the Vietnamese version than in the US.
+ The broth is richer, sweeter and more cloudy
+ Thicker noodle
+ Less spring onion. More brown/white onion
+ NO dough stick. Generous amount of vegetable & herb side dish
+ Table condiments: Hoisin, chili sauce (mostly off-the-shelf product), chili oil & fresh chili

Other notes:
- Phở Gà (Chicken Pho) is considered to be a completely different dish: The broth is made from chicken bone (not beef), using minimal amount of anise & cinnamon, but more ginger & shallot. Results in a very clear, more aromatic but less herby broth compare to the beef Pho. Lime leaves (shredded) is a MUST and give Phở Gà its unique aroma and taste. In Vietnam, a proper Pho shop will NOT sell Beef Pho and Chicken Pho together. Chicken Pho is a Northern specialty, most owners of Chicken Pho shop in the South are Northern immigrants
- Phở Thìn (@8:27) is not traditional and has its own unique style: using stir-fried beef instead of raw/cooked beef, results in a very smoky & rich, somewhat oily flavour. And yes, an insane amount of spring onion.
- It's hard to believe but you won't find any Sriracha sauce (yes, that famous rooster bottle!) in any Pho shop in Vietnam. In fact, most Vietnamese do not know about its existence.

I’m a Vietnamese and this is my comment about the Vietnamese ‘Phở’.
There are signification different of Phở among 3 locations, Phở in North Vietnam (Hanoi), South Vietnam (Saigon) and Phở in the United States and the world.
Phở in North Vietnam (Hanoi): The flavor is the best, but the taste is the worst due to lack of Beef Bones.
Phở in South Vietnam (Saigon): The flavor is not smell good as in North Vietnam but the taste is much better.
Phở in the United States and the world: The flavor is not smell good as in North Vietnam, and the taste is acceptable just because ‘fast foods McDonald cooking style’ instead of ‘family cooking’.

comments.text:
I met a Vietnamese retired lawyer man and his family in 1994 in San Jose, but this story happened during an annual business training in Daytona, FL.  His family invited me in private beside business functions in that week. 
When we started to eat their food, I asked the ingredients and food processes, so he DIDN'T bother to explain the details of the ingredients and the rest (he talked a lot in general and we were hungry, so it would take a long time😂), so he just said: 
"Aimé, you have 3,000 years of wisdom on your plate; Enjoy".
I never forget his love of Vietnamese food and this sentence.

I have many interesting stories with Vietnamese PHO restaurant owners, once in Abidjan and the rest in the US (some spoke French, others were trained in France in the '70s, esp. naval training).

Vietnamese coffee is on another level 🇻🇳☕ Today, I’m learning how to make three of Vietnam’s most famous coffees: egg coffee, coconut coffee, and salt coffee!

Vietnam has one of the most unique coffee cultures in the world, and Vietnamese coffee goes way beyond the traditional cà phê sữa đá. From the thick, creamy texture of Vietnamese egg coffee (cà phê trứng) to refreshing coconut coffee (cà phê cốt dừa) and the sweet and salty combination of Vietnamese salt coffee (cà phê muối), I wanted to learn how these famous drinks are actually made.

In this video, we make and try:

☕ Vietnamese Egg Coffee (Cà Phê Trứng)
🥥 Vietnamese Coconut Coffee (Cà Phê Cốt Dừa)

meta.title: Top 10 Must Try Vietnamese Foods 🇻🇳  || Vietnam Best Street Food & Traditional Dishes!
meta.description:
Top 10 Must Try Vietnamese Foods 🇻🇳  || Vietnam Best Street Food & Traditional Dishes!

Vietnam is a food lover's paradise, offering a diverse culinary experience packed with fresh ingredients, vibrant flavors, and aromatic herbs. From iconic street food to rich traditional dishes, Vietnamese cuisine reflects its deep cultural heritage. Here are the top 10 most popular foods in Vietnam that you must try!
Vietnam is famous for its rich culinary heritage, offering a perfect blend of flavors, textures, and fresh ingredients. From bustling street food stalls to fine dining restaurants, Vietnamese cuisine caters to every taste. In this video, we introduce you to the top 10 most popular Vietnamese dishes that showcase the country’s unique food culture.
One of the most iconic dishes is Pho, a flavorful noodle soup made with beef (Pho Bo) or chicken (Pho Ga). The broth, simmered for hours with bones, star anise, and cinnamon, creates a rich and aromatic flavor. Topped with fresh herbs, lime, and chili, Pho is a must-try dish that represents the soul of Vietnamese cuisine.
Another favorite is Banh Mi, a Vietnamese baguette sandwich that combines crispy French bread with flavorful fillings such as pate, grilled meats, pickled vegetables, and fresh cilantro. A perfect on-the-go meal, Banh Mi showcases the fusion of Vietnamese and French culinary influences.
For a fresh and healthy option, Goi Cuon, or fresh spring rolls, are a great choice. These delicate rice paper rolls are filled with shrimp, pork, vermicelli noodles, and fresh herbs, served with a peanut-hoisin dipping sauce. Light and flavorful, they are a perfect snack or appetizer.
If you’re visiting Hanoi, Bun Cha is a must-try dish. It consists of grilled pork patties and pork belly served with vermicelli noodles, fresh herbs, and a sweet-savory dipping sauce. This dish gained international recognition when former U.S. President Barack Obama enjoyed it during his Vietnam visit.
In Southern Vietnam, Com Tam (broken rice) is a popular dish. Typically served with a grilled pork chop, fried egg, shredded pork skin, and pickled vegetables, it is drizzled with a flavorful fish sauce-based dressing. This simple yet satisfying meal is a staple in Vietnamese cuisine.

meta.description:
Ninh Binh es uno de los lugares más espectaculares de Vietnam y, sin duda, una parada imprescindible en cualquier viaje por el país 🇻🇳

En este vídeo te enseño qué ver y qué hacer en Ninh Binh, visitando algunos de sus lugares más impresionantes:

🏯 El complejo espiritual de Bai Dinh, el mayor templo budista de Vietnam
⛰️ Las famosas Mua Caves, con una de las mejores vistas del país
🚣‍♂️ Paseo en barca por Trang An, Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la UNESCO
🎬 Los decorados naturales donde se rodó King Kong: Skull Island

Ninh Binh es conocida como la Bahía de Halong terrestre, y después de verla entenderás perfectamente por qué. Montañas kársticas, arrozales infinitos y paisajes que parecen sacados de otro planeta.

👉 Si estás organizando un viaje a Vietnam o buscas inspiración para tu próxima aventura, este vídeo te va a venir de lujo.

meta.title: Vietnam Food Tour As A Vegetarian | The Solo Female Traveller Ep 23 | Curly Tales
meta.description:
On my recent trip to Vietnam, the constant question I was battling as a vegetarian was - what are my options for food? To my surprise, I managed to try out some vegetarian dishes in Vietnam and gave my rating. Here's how it went! 

Vietnam is synonymous with the variety of seafood, banh mi and coffee. Although, ever wondered what it's like being a vegetarian here? Well let me tell you, it wasn't all that bad! There were a host of options to indulge in that went beyond the Aloo, Paneer and Mushroom window. 

So from the Vietnamese Ban Trang Nuoung, Noodles, Ché To Rice Paper Spring Roll and The Purple Lady Dessert, these were some of the top vegetarian delicacies that satisfied and pleased my taste buds and hunger pangs. Of course the rating is purely based on personal taste & experience and nothing more! 

Which dish are you most likely to taste? Let us know below!

meta.title: Exploring Marble Mountains Da Nang Vietnam | Full Tour
meta.description:
Explore the stunning Marble Mountains in Da Nang, Vietnam, one of the most famous and spiritual attractions in central Vietnam. In this video, I take you through ancient caves, beautiful Buddhist pagodas, scenic viewpoints, and hidden paths inside the Marble Mountains.

Located just a few kilometers from Da Nang city, Marble Mountains are known for their limestone peaks, marble caves, sacred temples, and panoramic views of the coastline. This video will help you understand what to see, how to reach, best time to visit, entry fee, and travel tips before you plan your trip.

Whether you’re a first-time traveler to Vietnam or exploring Da Nang tourist places, Marble Mountains is a must-visit destination.

📍 Location: Da Nang, Vietnam
🕍 Highlights: Huyen Khong Cave, Linh Ung Pagoda, viewpoints
⏰ Best time to visit: Morning or late afternoon

If you enjoy Vietnam travel videos, don’t forget to like, share, and subscribe for more travel vlogs and hidden gems.

meta.title: Train from Da Nang to Hue|Which side of the train should you get? (+Visiting Hue Imperial City)
meta.description:
Come along with me as I take one of the most scenic train rides in the world! In this video, I’m traveling from Da Nang to Hue aboard the train via the famous Hai Van Pass, where the mountains meet the ocean with incredible coastal views. 

Once we arrive in Hue, we head straight to explore the historic Imperial City (Hue Citadel), diving into the rich culture, grand architecture, and royalty history of Vietnam. If you're planning a trip to Central Vietnam or just love travel vlogs, I hope this video gives you a good look at what the experience is like! 

Don't forget to hit like, leave a comment, and subscribe for more travel adventures!

comments.text: I would say tips are expected in Vietnam now. For example, when you take a boat trip in Ninh Binh, the standard tip should be VND 50,000 VND~ 1.8$ for boat man. For cyclo, the tip should be VND 50,000 VND~ 1.8$ for cyclo drivers. Cyclo drivers in Hanoi and Hue may ask you directly for tipping which it's not nice in some cases. Thus, in order to avoid awkward situation, you can give tip right after services. It's a small amount when you consider the low income of the labour in Vietnam and how hard they work under the weather.

transcript: Vietnam. What's the first thing that comes to your mind? Hanoi, lanterns, con hats, street food, Saigon, egg, coffee, history, rice fields, temples, Harlong Bay or train street? Everyone has their own bucket list. And on this list, Vietnam ranks among the best. I have lived, worked, and traveled this beautiful, diverse country for over 7 months, and now I want to share my knowledge and experience with you. This is how I would spend 14 days in Vietnam. You will be either arriving in Ho Chi Min or Hanoi. For the sake of simplicity, we start from Hanoi. No worries. This journey works also in reverse. Our journey begins in the lively streets of Hanoi, where the pulse of the city sets the tone for our Vietnam exploration. From Hanoi, we embark on a night bus to Sappa, nestled in the majestic mountains of northern Vietnam, surrounded by verdant rice terraces and the warm hospitality of the local hill tribes. Next, we journey by night bus to Catbar, a picturesque island, where we will do a road trip across the island by motorbike. Our next destination is the legendary Harlong Bay, where we spend a night aboard a cruise ship, sailing among the iconic limestone formations and soaking in its enchanting beauty. Continuing our adventure, we explore the tranquil beauty of Tamco in Ning Bin, also known as the Harlong Bay on land, where towering limestone rise from the emerald waters. Then we head to Hanoi to take a flight to Hui, the former imperial capital of Vietnam, where we delve into the rich history and cultural heritage of the region. From here, we take the train to Daang, a vibrant city on the central coast of Vietnam. 25 minutes away is Hoyan. We explore the ancient streets where lanterns sway gently in the breeze and history comes to life at every turn. Our adventure reaches its peak in the vibrant metropolis of Ho Chi Min City, also known as Saigon, where we discover the energy and excitement of urban life in Vietnam's largest city. Some information you will need before arriving in Vietnam. Best time to visit Vietnam depends on what you want to explore. Northern Vietnam, April to June and September to December. Early October for the green rice terraces. Central Vietnam, February to May. South Vietnam, November to April for dry season. Mentioning these, April should be your goal to go if you want to see all the country. Lastly, at the end of the video, we will break down how much this trip will cost you and show you an alternative budget friendly route if you have more time to spend in Vietnam. Arriving Hanoi, the heart and soul of Vietnam, where you can lose yourself in the chaotic charm of the old quarter. Here are some places to visit. Stroll around the labyrinthine streets of the old quarter and wander through its narrow streets filled with ancient charm and vibrant shops. Try Hanoi's unique and famous egg coffee at the iconic cafe jam, the birthplace of this amazing tasting coffee. Get a customtailored suit crafted by skilled craftsmen in the heart of Hanoi, all within a swift 24-hour time frame. Experience serenity amidst the bustling city by strolling around the picturesque Hong Kim Lake. Home to the historic Nox Sun Temple nestled on its tranquil waters. [Music] Explore the night market at Han Kim Lake. Join locals and fellow travelers alike at Beer Street. Unwind and recharge at Loading Tea Cafe. A cozy spot where vintage decor and aromatic coffee create the perfect ambiance for a leisurely morning. Check out the spectacle of the famous Train Street, where cafes stand just inches away from passing trains, creating a truly unique and mesmerizing experience. Treat your taste buds to the flavors of Vietnam with a mouthwatering banani sandwich, steaming bowl of faux noodle soup, or dectable king rotty pastry. Each offering a unique culinary experience. From Hanoi, we venture north to the picturesque town of Sappa. Best way to reach Sappa is via night bus from Hanoi. It will take you around 6 hours to arrive. Trek through stunning rice terraces, visit local villages, and immerse yourself in the rich culture of the ethnic minority groups. [Music] [Applause] Hop on a night bus to Catbar Island, a hidden gem that is less touristic than the bigger brother Harlong Bay. Here you can rent a bike and do a road trip across the island in just an hour. You can make some stops along the way for mesmerizing views. Next, we set sail to the emerald waters of Halong Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Cruise past limestone casts rising from the sea. [Music] Explore hidden caves. Go kayaking. and soak in the serenity of this otherworldly landscape. Traveling inland, we discover the serene beauty of Tamco, often referred to as Halong Bay on land. Embark on a serene boat journey along the river, where towering limestone casts and lush greenery create a breathtaking backdrop for your adventure. Ascend to the summit of Hangmua, where a challenging hike rewards you with panoramic views of Tamco's stunning scenery, including its iconic dragon statue. [Music] Explore the beauty of Tamcock. Wander through its picturesque landscapes and charming villages at your own pace. Whether by zipping through on a motorbike or leisurely pedaling on a bicycle. Step into a world of tranquility and spirituality as you visit Beach Dong Pagoda. From here we go back to Hanoi airport to take a flight to Hugh. Delve into the country's rich history as you explore the majestic imperial city, ancient citadels, and ornate pagodas. [Music] Our journey continues south to the coastal city of Da. Here you can relax on pristine beaches after an exhausting trip in the north. Don't miss the iconic Dragon Bridge, though. Ever since completion in 2013, a fire and water show has been held twice weekly on Saturday and Sunday. Take the chance to visit Bana Hills theme park with its iconic Golden Bridge. [Music] Just a short drive from Daang lies the charming town of Hoyan, a UNESCO World Heritage site renowned for its colorful architecture and lantern lit streets. [Music] Heat. Heat. N. [Music] Yeah. [Music] Our journey concludes in the bustling metropolis of Saigon, also known as Ho Chi Min City. [Music] Dive into the vibrant street life. [Music] Visit historic landmarks such as the Notream Cathedral of Saigon [Music] and do a day trip to Mikong Delta. [Music] I really packed a lot of things into this itinerary because I want to inspire you to have the best time you can. But not to worry if it's too tight a schedule. You can just pick up the things that you like the most and drop those if you didn't. Feel free to tweak any parts to better fit your vision or add any additional details you'd like to highlight about each location. As promised here, the alternative budget friendly route, you could do the whole trip by bus and train as shown in the map. This will take more time. However, if you do it right, you could save up to 70% on accommodation and transportation. For the train, you can book your tickets via the official Vietnamese rail website. If you choose to stay longer, you can add Fukuquok to your list. Fukuquok is a tropical paradise known for its stunning beaches, crystal clear waters, and lush jungles. transcript: साउथ ईस्ट एशिया की एक ऐसी कंट्री जो बाली के बीचेस, थाईलैंड की नाइट लाइफ, स्विट्जरलैंड का माउंटेन और यूरोप का कल्चर एक साथ ऑफर करता है। वह भी हाफ बजट में। अगर आपने वियतनाम प्लान नहीं किया तो 2025 का हॉटेस्ट डेस्टिनेशन आप मिस कर रहे हैं। वियतनाम की ट्रिप प्लान करना थोड़ा ट्रिकी हो सकता है क्योंकि यह कंट्री काफी बड़ी है। पर टेंशन मत लो। मैं आपको बताने वाला हूं कैसे सिर्फ 50 से 6,000 में बेस्ट ट्रिप आप प्लान कर सकते हैं। तो चलिए शुरू करते हैं। हे गाइस, दिस इज शशांक एंड वेलकम बैक टू माय चैनल। आई होप यू आर डूइंग अब्सोलुटली गुड। मैं इस वीडियो में आप लोगों को वियतनाम की कंप्लीट आइटनरी बताने वाला हूं जो 7, 10, 13 और 15 दिन की होने वाली है। अगर आप लोग साउथ टू नॉर्थ ट्रैवल करना चाह रहे हैं या नॉर्थ टू साउथ ट्रैवल करना चाह रहे हैं। तो हम लोग इसमें बात करेंगे फ्लाइट वीजा आप कैसे प्रोसेस करा सकते हैं? इंश्योरेंस आप कौन सा लें? सिम कहां से ले सकते हैं? करेंसी एक्सचेंज के बारे में बताने वाला हूं। लोकल ट्रांसपोर्ट के बारे में बताने वाला हूं। अकोमोडेशन के बारे में बताने वाला हूं। कौन सी-कौ सी एप्लीकेशन आप लोग इंस्टॉल करके आए? फिर लोकल लैंग्वेज कौन सा है? फिर बेस्ट टाइम क्या है? फ़ूड ऑप्शंस फिर सीनियर सिटीजन के क्या चैलेंजेस हैं? यहां पर व्हीलचेयर की फैसिलिटी है कि नहीं है। फिर सबसे मेन चीज थिंग्स टू कैरी आपको बताने वाला हूं। और लास्ट में एक प्रॉपर बजट समरी बताने वाला हूं। तो आप लोग इस वीडियो में बने रहिए मेरे साथ और देखते रहिए मेरे चैनल को और सब्सक्राइब नहीं किया है तो जरूर सब्सक्राइब करिए। सबसे पहले जान लेते हैं हाउ टू रीच। इंडिया से वियतनाम के लिए दिल्ली, मुंबई, कोलकाता, अहमदाबाद, बेंगलुरु और हैदराबाद से डायरेक्ट फ्लाइट अवेलेबल हैं। हनोय, दनांग और होचीमिन सिटी में मेजर इंटरनेशनल एयरपोर्ट है। वेजेट और वियतनाम एयरलाइंस की राउंड ट्रिप फ्लाइट 15,000 से 20,000 में मिल जाती है। अगर आप दो-ती महीने बुक करेंगे पहले तो। मुझे 19,000 में फ्लाइट मिली थी जिसमें मैंने 15 केजी एक्स्ट्रा बैगेज भी इंक्लूड कराया था। VJet एयरलाइंस बजट फ्रेंडली है लेकिन कंफर्ट थोड़ा कम मिलेगा। बेस्ट फेयर के लिए स्काई स्कैनर या एयरलाइन की ऑफिशियल वेबसाइट से कंपेयर करके ही बुक करें। अभी बात कर लेते हैं वीजा और ट्रैवल इंश्योरेंस की। वियतनाम का वीजा प्रोसेस काफी सिंपल है। यहां आपको ई वीजा मिलता है। सिंगल या मल्टीपल एंट्री जो 90 दिन तक वैलिड रहता है। वीजा ऑन अराइवल यहां पर अवेलेबल नहीं होता है। आप ऑफिशियल वियतनाम इमीग्रेशन वेबसाइट से $25 में ई वीजा अप्लाई कर सकते हैं। आप अप्लाई करने के लिए आपको एंट्री एग्जिट डेट्स, होटल एड्रेस, पासपोर्ट डिटेल्स और बेसिक इंफॉर्मेशन चाहिए रहती है। प्रोसेसिंग टाइम बेसिकली चार से पांच दिन होता है। बट आप लोग 2 वीक पहले ही इसको अप्लाई करें और स्कैम अवॉइड करने के लिए सिर्फ ऑफिशियल लिंक से ही अप्लाई करें। डिस्क्रिप्शन में मैं ऑफिशियल लिंक डाल दूंगा। ई वीजा अप्रूवल लेटर का प्रिंट आउट लेके पासपोर्ट के साथ इमीग्रेशन पे दिखाएं और आप वियतनाम एंट्री कर सकते हैं। अभी ट्रैवल इंश्योरेंस की बात करते हैं तो वियतनाम के लिए इंश्योरेंस मैंडेटरी नहीं है बट हाईली रिकमेंडेड है। मेडिकल इमरजेंसीज या बैगेज लॉस या ट्रिप कैंसिलेशन से बचने के लिए इंश्योरेंस जरूर लेना चाहिए और आप जरूर लेना। इंश्योरेंस 300 से ₹800 में आपको 5 से 10 लाख तक का कवरेज वाला आराम से मिल जाएगा। अगर आप लोगों को इंश्योरेंस कंपेयर करना है तो पॉलिसी बा या मेक माय ट्रिप आप लोग यूज कर सकते हैं। अभी बात कर लेते हैं मनी एक्सचेंज की। तो वियतनाम में वियतनामीज़ डोंग चलता है जिसका एक्सचेंज रेट स्क्रीन पर आप लोगों को दिख रहा होगा। करेंसी कैरी करने के यहां पर दो बेस्ट ऑप्शन है। अगर आप कैश ले जा रहे हैं तो अमेरिकन डॉलर कैरी करें और और $ के बड़े नोट प्रेफर करें क्योंकि बड़े नोट से बेटर एक्सचेंज रेट्स आपको यहां मिलता है। वियतनाम में यूएसडी का एक्सचेंज रेट इंडिया के कंपैरिजन में काफी अच्छा है। तो इंडिया से डायरेक्टली डोंग लेके ना आं। एयरपोर्ट पर सिर्फ 50 से $ डोंग में कन्वर्ट करवा लें ताकि टैक्सी या बेसिक आपको जो खर्चा है वह कवर हो सके। बाकी एक्सचेंज सिटी में ही करें। तीन-चार शॉप कंपेयर करके और बेस्ट रेट आपको गोल्ड शॉप पे ही मिलेगा। दूसरा ऑप्शन कार्ड्स है। अगर आप फॉररेक्स कार्ड, इंटरनेशनल डेबिट क्रेडिट कार्ड या न्यू कार्ड यूज करते हैं तो न्यू कार्ड जो है वह बेस्ट ऑप्शन है क्योंकि इसका लोएस्ट कन्वर्शन चार्जेस लगता है लाइक एक या 2% व्हिच इज ओके। वियतनाम में एटीएम ईली अवेलेबल है और मेजर रेस्टोरेंट्स और शॉपिंग सेंटर में कार्ड पेमेंट भी एक्सेप्टेड है। अभी सिम की बात कर लेते हैं। तो वियतनाम में सिम एयरपोर्ट से आप बिल्कुल ना लें क्योंकि यहां ऑलमोस्ट 2x प्राइस चार्ज करते हैं। बेस्ट ऑप्शन Virtel का ऑफिशियल स्टोर है जो होइकिम लेक के सामने अवेलेबल है। मैं वो लोकेशन नीचे डिस्क्रिप्शन में डाल दूंगा। जहां Virtel का 4 से 5GB पर डे वाला डाटा पैक आपको ₹500 ₹600 में आराम से मिल जाता है। अभी होटल और अकोमोडेशन की बात कर लेते हैं। वियतनाम में हर टाइप का बजट और कंफर्ट के अकॉर्डिंग स्टे ऑप्शंस अवेलेबल हैं। हर सिटी में बेस्ट लोकेशन में होटल बुक करने के लिए इंपॉर्टेंट यही है कि आप लोग सिटी के सेंटर में होटल बुक करें और जिससे आपको टूरिस्ट लोकेशन आसपास पड़े और शॉपिंग और फूड ऑप्शंस भी आपको ईजीली अवेलेबल हो पाए। अगर आप लो बजट में ट्रैवल कर रहे हैं तो हॉस्टल आप लोगों के लिए बेस्ट ऑप्शन रहेगा। ₹500 से ₹600 में आराम से एक बंक बेड मिल जाता है। आप बुकिंग ऑप्शन पे चेक कर सकते हैं। यहां पर काफी हॉस्टल्स अवेलेबल रहते हैं। कंफर्ट और अफोर्डेबिलिटी का बैलेंस चाहिए तो आप लोग होटल ले सकते हैं जो ₹100 से ₹2000 पर नाइट में आपको डबल ऑक्यूुपेंसी आसानी से मिल जाएगा। यहां पर आपको बहुत ऑप्शंस मिलेंगे होटल के। अगर आप सेल्फ कुकिंग करना चाहते हैं या वीगन जेन फूड प्रेफर करते हैं तो एयरबीnबी बेस्ट ऑप्शन रहेगा। यहां 2 से ₹3000 में आपको एयरबीnबी फुल्ली इक्विप्ड अपार्टमेंट मिल जाता है। हमने भी एयरबीnबी ही लिया था। अभी लोकल ट्रांसपोर्टेशन की बात कर लेते हैं। तो पूरे वियतनाम में आपको सेल्फ ड्राइव बाइक, गैब कार जैसे अपनी Ola और Uber होता है इंडिया में। गैब बाइक जैसे रेपिडो बाइक इंडिया में होता है और लोकल बसेस के ऑप्शन मिल जाते हैं। सबसे बजट फ्रेंडली जो ऑप्शन है वह आप लोग सेल्फ ड्राइव स्कूटी जो है वह रेंट कर सकते हैं। ₹500 पर डे के हिसाब से आपको मिल जाएगी या आप लोग लोकल बसेस में भी ट्रैवल कर सकते हैं। ₹40-50 लेते हैं या आप लोग गैब बाइक भी यूज कर सकते हैं जो एक राइड का ₹80 ₹100 लेते हैं। गैब टैक्सी थोड़ी हाईली चार्ज है। बट अगर आप लोग चार-प लोगों के ग्रुप में आ रहे हैं तो वह बजट में हो जाता है। अभी कुछ एप्स हैं जो आप लोग जरूर इंस्टॉल करके आं। यह आपको स्क्रीन पे दिख रही होंगी। अभी लोकल लैंग्वेज की बात कर लेते हैं। तो वियतनाम में वियतनामीज़ लैंग्वेज चलती है। बट यहां पर आपको लैंग्वेज की थोड़ी बहुत प्रॉब्लम होने वाली है क्योंकि इंग्लिश काफी कम लोगों को यहां पर आती है। तो आप लोग Google ट्रांसलेट ऑफलाइन वाला जरूर डाउनलोड करके यहां पर आं क्योंकि आपको हर जगह उसकी जरूरत पड़ने वाली है। अभी फूड ऑप्शन की बात कर लेते हैं। अगर आप नॉन वेजिटेरियन है तो आपके लिए यहां पर काफी ऑप्शंस अवेलेबल हैं। लाइक सी फूड, चिकन, पोक, मटन इसके अलावा भी काफी कुछ और मिल जाता है। और अगर आप वेजिटेरियन या जैन फूड प्रेफर करते हैं तो बिल्कुल भी डरने की जरूरत नहीं है। यहां आपको काफी इंडियन रेस्टोरेंट्स मिल जाएंगे। इंडियन खाना थोड़ा एक्सपेंसिव है यहां पर। बट दो लोगों का अराउंड ₹1000 ₹1500 में आपको मिल जाएगा। और अगर आप एयरबीयन भी ले रहे हैं तो आप इंडिया से कुकिंग का सामान कैरी कर सकते हैं। और यहां कुक भी कर सकते हैं जो हमने किया था। अगर आपको एयरबीnबी से रिलेटेड सारी इंफॉर्मेशन चाहिए तो कमेंट में बता देना। इफ द कमेंट्स आर मोर आई विल मेक अ सेपरेट वीडियो ऑन एयरबीएनबी। और मैंने क्या कैरी किया इंडिया से और क्या ₹600 से ₹1000 पर डे में हो जाता है। ट्रांसपोर्टेशन की बात करते हैं तो बसेस, ट्रेंस या आप टू व्हीलर रेंट करते हैं तो ₹300 से ₹600 पर डे लगता है उसमें और इंटरनल फ्लाइट्स की बात करते हैं तो वह थोड़ा कॉस्टली है। तो ₹1500 से ₹4000 लगेगा। आप लोग इंटरनल में बस भी ले सकते हैं और ट्रेन भी ले सकते हैं। अभी टूर्स और टिकट की बात करते हैं तो 7 दिन के टूर के लिए आपको 8 से ₹10,000 लगेगा। टोटल एस्टीमेट की बात करते हैं तो 7 दिन अगर आप लोग रुकेंगे तो 40 से ₹00 लगेगा। अभी आइटनरी की बात करते हैं। 7 दिन की आइटनरी मैंने आपको ऑलरेडी बता दी है। 10 दिन में आप लोग सापा इंक्लूड कर लीजिए। अगर आप 13 डेज की आइटनरी की बात करते हैं तो आप लोग फकॉक इंक्लूड करें। इसमें साफा मत करें। 15 दिन की आइडिनरी की बात करते हैं तो आप लोग साफा और दोनों इंक्लूड कर सकते हैं। अगर आप लोगों को 7 10 13 15 दिन की कंप्लीट डिटेल्ड आइटनरी चाहिए विद कॉस्ट ब्रेकडाउन तो आप लोग कमेंट में आइटनरी लिखिए। मैं आप लोगों को आइटनरी भेज दूंगा। हमारा यहीं पर खत्म होता है। आई होप आप लोगों को यह वीडियो अच्छा लगा होगा। अगर अच्छा लगा हो तो लाइक, शेयर करिए, सब्सक्राइब करिए चैनल को और बने रहिए मेरे साथ हमेशा के लिए। थैंक यू सो मच फॉर वाचिंग। मिलते हैं दूसरे वीडियो में नेक्स्ट डेस्टिनेशन में। बाय-ब टेक केयर। [संगीत]

meta.title: 4 Days in Northern Vietnam 🇻🇳 The Perfect Itinerary: Hanoi, Ninh Binh & Ha Long Bay
meta.description:
Hello everyone, welcome back to GADT Travel! 👋

Planning a trip to **Northern Vietnam in just 4 days**? 🇻🇳 From the charming streets of Hanoi to the spectacular limestone mountains of Ninh Binh and the emerald waters of Ha Long Bay, this itinerary brings together some of the most unforgettable experiences in northern Vietnam.

In this video, we're taking you on a **4-day Northern Vietnam adventure**, combining local culture, historic landmarks, breathtaking natural scenery, delicious Vietnamese food, and an amazing cruise experience.

✨ Here's what you can experience on this 4-day journey:

🏙️ Explore Hanoi – Wander through the Old Quarter, visit Hoan Kiem Lake, experience the unique Hanoi Train Street, and enjoy the city's lively street food and café culture.

🚣 Discover Ninh Binh – Visit Hoa Lu Ancient Capital, take a scenic boat ride through the spectacular limestone landscapes of Trang An, and climb Mua Cave for panoramic views over the rivers and rice fields.

⛵ Cruise through Ha Long Bay – Sail among dramatic limestone islands, enjoy a Vietnamese lunch on board, explore an impressive natural cave, and experience kayaking or a traditional bamboo boat ride, depending on the cruise itinerary and weather conditions.

🏛️ Discover More of Hanoi – If your departure schedule allows, explore Hanoi's historical landmarks, including the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex, One Pillar Pagoda, and Temple of Literature, before heading to the airport.

This 4-day Vietnam itinerary is ideal for travelers who want to experience the highlights of Northern Vietnam without spending too much time traveling between destinations. It's a wonderful combination of city life, cultural discoveries, nature, and adventure.

Wondering **what to do in Hanoi, how to explore Ninh Binh, or whether a Ha Long Bay cruise is worth adding to your trip?** Follow along for inspiration and ideas to help plan your Vietnam adventure!

meta.title: Hoi An Ancient Town, Vietnam (January 2025)
meta.description:
Hoi An is an ancient town located along the Thu Bon River in central Vietnam, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999. It was a major Southeast Asian trading port from the 15th to the 19th century, where merchants from Japan, China, and Europe exchanged goods such as silk, ceramics, and spices.

The town's architecture is a blend of Vietnamese, Japanese, Chinese, and French influences, preserved in wooden shop houses, tiled roofs, and narrow alleys. The iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, built in the 16th century, symbolizes centuries of cultural exchange. Hoi An's grid-like street plan reflects its historical mercantile function and features over 1,000 timber-framed buildings. 

Seasonal flooding from the Thu Bon River has shaped local building techniques, including elevated floors and flood-adapted storefronts. Traditional crafts like lantern-making, woodcarving, and tailoring continue to thrive, supporting a living heritage economy.

நான் புவனி தரன், பேக் பேக்கர், ஹிட்சிகர், வோல்கர் & ட்ரெக்கர், உலகம் முழுவதும் பயணம் செய்து எனது அனுபவங்களை அனைவருடனும் பகிர்ந்து கொள்கிறேன்.

புதிய இடங்களைப் பார்ப்பது, வெவ்வேறு கலாச்சாரத்தை அனுபவிப்பது, மக்களைப் பற்றி அறிந்து கொள்வது, இந்த அழகான உலகத்தை தமிழ் ட்ரெக்கர் வழியாக உங்களுக்குக் காட்ட முயற்சிப்பேன்.

எனது இந்த பயணத்தில் அனைவரையும் வெளியே செல்லவும், ஆராயவும், அவர்கள் சந்திக்கும் ஒவ்வொரு சூழ்நிலையையும் சிறப்பாகப் பயன்படுத்தவும் ஊக்குவிப்பதாகும்.

I'm Bhuvani Dharan, Solo travel enthusiast, Backpacker, hitchhiker, vlogger & trekker who travels the world and shares my experiences with everyone.

My videos consist of my spontaneous everyday life as each day is a new adventure.

Love to see new places, experience different culture, learn about people, taste different food and more. I will try to show you this beautiful world via Tamil Trekker.

With an emphasis on traveling these vlogs are meant to encourage everyone to go out, explore & make the most out of every situation they come across.

Hello everyone, welcome back to GADT Travel! 👋

Planning a trip to Da Nang, Vietnam? 🇻🇳 One of the most common questions travelers ask is: When is the best time to visit Da Nang?

In this video, we'll help you choose the perfect season for your trip by covering Da Nang's weather throughout the year, including the dry season, rainy season, temperatures, and the best months to visit based on your travel plans.

Whether you're looking forward to relaxing on My Khe Beach, exploring Ba Na Hills, wandering through Hoi An, or enjoying the city's famous bridges, knowing the best time to visit will help you make the most of your journey.

🎥 In this video, you'll learn:

🌞 The best months to visit Da Nang

🌧️ What to expect during the rainy season

🌡️ Weather and temperatures throughout the year

🏖️ The best time for beaches and outdoor activities

💡 Travel tips for first-time visitors

Da Nang is one of Vietnam's most beautiful coastal destinations, offering stunning beaches, breathtaking mountain views, delicious local food, and easy access to Hoi An and Hue. No matter when you visit, this guide will help you plan the perfect trip.

✨ Planning your Vietnam adventure?

At GADT Travel, we specialize in customized Vietnam tours tailored to your travel style, interests, and budget. Whether you're exploring Da Nang, Hoi An, Ba Na Hills, Hue, or traveling across Vietnam, our local experts are here to help you create the perfect itinerary.

Don't forget to LIKE 👍, SUBSCRIBE 🔔, and turn on notifications for more Vietnam travel guides, seasonal travel tips, and authentic local experiences with GADT Travel.

Experience the best of Southern Vietnam in 7 days with this complete travel itinerary. From the modern, chaotic streets of Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) to the cooler, cozy atmosphere of Da Lat, this guide shows you two completely different sides of Vietnam.

After spending over a year living and traveling across Vietnam, I’ve put together this itinerary based on real experiences — including cafés, temples, local food, hidden spots, and everyday moments.

Explore Saigon’s cafés, apartment buildings, Book Street, and temples

comments.author: @gotripAI-com
comments.text:
Watched the full video and Phu Quoc - it looks incredible! For anyone planning a trip there, here are the absolute must-see highlights from this vlog:

00:00:10 - That seafood spread is next level. Freshness is 10/10 there.
00:06:00 - Pro Tip: Most of these stalls are cash-only, so hit the ATM before you enter!
00:16:09 - The Vietnamese Pizza (Bánh Tráng Nướng) is a must-try street snack.
00:24:31 - Don't skip the rolled ice cream—it's as much a performance as it is a dessert.

Quick heads up for travelers: PQC airport is very strict about not allowing Fish Sauce (Nước Mắm) in carry-on, so pack it in your checked bag or buy it at the duty-free! Safe travels everyone.

meta.title: Vietnam's 1,500-Year Empire Lost To History: Living Relics Of Champa Kingdom | The Mark Of Empire
meta.description:
Linked to ancient seafarers from Taiwan, the Champa were expert sailors and vital players in global trade. On land, they were skilled builders and innovative agriculturalists who also made their mark on the modern world. Curator and scholar Peter Lee embarks on a quest to uncover the story of the Champa Kingdom and its glory years.

From visiting the ancient, hallowed grounds of My Son Sanctuary where grand temples showcase the king’s authority, to learning about modern Cham identity with a local rap artist, Peter traces the great heights that the kingdom reached before its eventual decline. But in recent years, a new generation of Cham people are striving for pride and recognition of their ancient heritage.

WATCH MORE The Mark of Empire: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLkMf14VQEvTbN1Gh3smAZtc2E-ACeu3Fg

03:06 Inside Hoi An's Marble Mountains
06:26 Fishing on traditional basket boats

==============================
ABOUT The Mark of Empire: Kingdoms of the Sea:
What are the secrets and mysteries behind Asia’s ancient empires? In the third season of this award-winning series, curator and scholar Peter Lee is back on a journey to trace clues and uncover new theories behind the Srivijaya empire, the Champa kingdom, the Sultanate of Sulu, and the Anuradhapura kingdom. What were the epic battles, political alliances and cultural exchanges forged by the four powers in the region?

From investigating the iconic reliefs of Borobudur temple in Indonesia, to diving for sea cucumbers in the Philippines’ Sulu Archipelago, to practicing the ancient martial art of Angampora in Sri Lanka, and learning about modern Cham rap music in Vietnam, Peter traces the rise and fall of these formidable kingdoms, and the cultural legacies that they have left on the region until today.

comments.author: @nguyentandat2001
comments.text:
As a Vietnamese person (ethnically Kinh), I want to speak frankly but respectfully to some foreign friends, especially Cham Muslims in Cambodia and parts of the Muslim community in Malaysia that claiming Cham heritage in Vietnam as “yours” lacks any serious academic basis. For most of its history, Champa was an Indianized kingdom, deeply shaped by Hinduism (Shaivism and Vaishnavism) and later Buddhism, with the Cham language belonging to the Austronesian family and a cultural identity distinct from the Malay–Islamic world.

In present-day Vietnam, the Cham community is officially recognized as having three main groups: Cham Bàlamôn (Ahiêr) and Cham Bàni (Awal), two long-established indigenous communities concentrated in Ninh Thuận and Bình Thuận, which are historically the heartland of Champa; and Cham Islam (orthodox Sunni), a later formation resulting from trade networks and Islamic missionary activities, mainly found in An Giang and parts of southern Vietnam. To attribute the entirety of Champa’s temples, art, religious practices, and customary laws to Islam or to “Malay culture” is a misrepresentation of history. Islam in the Cham context is a later layer of cultural adaptation, not the civilizational foundation of Champa. Mutual respect must begin with respect for historical facts: Champa’s heritage belongs to the Cham people, is preserved in Vietnam, and cannot be appropriated through oversimplified narratives or contemporary identity politics.

comments.text:
I was quite interested in Vietnam history  before I travel to Vietnam recently. 
It may surprise many, but I believe the Campa people could have Indian or even Sri Lankan origins. In Sri Lanka, the worship of Lord Shiva dates back to very ancient times. Long ago, the Naga clan — one of the earliest known Sri Lankan communities — lived as skilled sea traders, connecting with many cultures around the world. Their symbol was the snake, which they proudly used as their emblem.

They were wealthy merchants who traded spices, pearls, gems, and metals. In ancient times, weaving was an important craft used to make clothing — something we also see in Cham culture. Even today, betel leaves and areca nut are used in auspicious events and when inviting priests, a tradition shared across many South and Southeast Asian cultures.

It is possible that one group of these prosperous sea merchants settled in a new land and eventually established their own kingdom. Later, with Chinese influence, their language, physical features, and cultural expressions may have evolved. However, ancestor worship is still practiced among many tribal communities, preserving a connection to the past.

No one can firmly claim a single origin, because the people of these regions are deeply mixed — influenced by Indian, Chinese, Arab, and later Western colonization. Original traditions naturally changed, and new traditions developed through these interactions. The same has happened to us in Sri Lanka. Some still argue about “pure origins,” without realizing that our own heritage has also been shaped by centuries of cultural exchange.

With globalization, cultures continue to change rapidly. The younger generation around the world often looks and lives similarly. Change is the ultimate reality. 😊❤

From there, we visited the picturesque Son Tra Marina, one of the most Instagram-worthy spots in the city, before ending our day exploring the incredible caves, temples, and viewpoints of Marble Mountains.

If you're planning a trip to Da Nang, these places are definitely worth adding to your itinerary!

📍 Places visited:
• Linh Ung Pagoda / Lady Buddha
• Son Tra Marina
• Marble Mountains

meta.title: 7 Tourist Scams in Vietnam and How to Avoid Them (Money Switching, Fake Taxis)
meta.description:
7 tourist scams in Vietnam target visitors every day — money switching, fake taxis, rigged meters. Learn how each works and exactly how to avoid it.

This 7-minute guide breaks down the seven most common tourist scams in Vietnam: money switching with confusing dong notes, fake taxis with rigged meters, shoe-shine and photo traps, market overcharging, cyclo price tricks and short-changing, fake tour agents, and ATM skimmers plus motorbike rental damage claims. For each scam you will see how it works, what it costs, and the exact fix that keeps your money safe.

meta.title: ULTIMATE Vietnamese Street Food Tour in Hoi An, Vietnam 🇻🇳 Most UNDERRATED Food City in Vietnam?
meta.description:
Ultimate Vietnamese street food tour in Hoi An, Vietnam. Is this the most underrated food city in Vietnam?

🔔 SUBSCRIBE FOR MORE FOOD ADVENTURES: https://www.youtube.com/HungryTwoTravel?sub_confirmation=1
👀 WATCH Vietnam Street Food: https://youtu.be/OwSAL3k-DRc

We started our Vietnamese street food tour of Hoi An to determine whether or not this is the most underrated food city in Vietnam. Our first stop was to taste the locally made rose dumplings, with four generations of delicious history! Next up was for a popular street food in Hoi An, grilled pork skewers, these were super flavourful and so tasty and charred.

Any Vietnamese street food tour in Hoi An has to include one of the most popular foods in Vietnam, cao lau. Cao lau is a very popular Vietnamese food that is only found in Hoi An, nowhere else in the country! We were blown away by how tasty and delicious it was. We tasted a local Vietnamese sweet soup, a popular Hoi An drink, as well as a jam packed banh mi. You can’t go to a new city without trying banh mi, the number one street food in Vietnam!

We finished off our ultimate Vietnamese street food tour in Hoi An, Vietnam, tasting the local chicken rice, and a very unique mango cake. With so many foods to eat in Hoi An, we had to make sure to hit up the best street food spots, and we’ve gotta say, the food did not disappoint!

We hope you enjoy our ultimate Vietnamese street food tour in Hoi An, Vietnam. So, what do you think, is Hoi An the most underrated food city in Vietnam? Stay tuned next week for more food adventures!

#vietnamesefood #vietnamstreetfood #hoian #vietnamfood #hộian #vietnam

meta.title: Da Nang’s Lady Buddha : Is it good?
meta.description:
🌸 Join us as we explore the incredible Lady Buddha (Linh Ung Pagoda) in Da Nang, Vietnam! 🌸

Located on the Son Tra Peninsula, the Lady Buddha statue is the tallest in Vietnam and a must-see landmark for anyone visiting Da Nang. In this video, we take you on a tour of the Linh Ung Pagoda, wander through peaceful courtyards filled with Buddhist statues, admire the stunning views of the East Sea, and meet some monkeys  

✨ What you’ll see in this video:
 • The towering Lady Buddha statue (67 meters high!)
 • Beautiful details of the Linh Ung Pagoda
 • Scenic views of Da Nang city and coastline
 • Peaceful gardens filled with Buddhist art & symbolism
 • Travel tips for visiting the Son Tra Peninsula

If you’re planning a trip to Vietnam, the Lady Buddha in Da Nang is one of the best things to do, and it’s perfect for culture lovers, photographers, and anyone seeking a peaceful escape from the city.

📍 Location: Linh Ung Pagoda, Son Tra Peninsula, Da Nang, Vietnam

Don’t forget to like 👍, comment 💬, and subscribe 🔔 for more Vietnam travel adventures!

meta.title: Walking Through Linh Ung Pagoda, Son Tra Peninsula | 4K Silent Walking Tour Da Nang
meta.description:
Walk with me through Linh Ung Pagoda — a sacred temple resting on Son Tra Peninsula, home to Vietnam's tallest Lady Buddha statue, overlooking the entire bay of Da Nang. This video has no narration and no added music — only the real sounds of the mountains: temple bells, wind, and the distant sea.

Linh Ung Pagoda is one of three famous "Linh Ung" temples in Da Nang, built on sacred ground where the Lady Buddha is said to have once appeared. Standing 67 meters tall among the clouds, the statue of Avalokiteshvara (Quan The Am Bo Tat) is one of Da Nang's most iconic landmarks — a place of both worship and quiet reflection.

📍 Location: Linh Ung Pagoda, Son Tra Peninsula, Da Nang, Vietnam
🔇 No Talking — Natural Sound Only

comments.text: Hi, is the package offered by Lily Travels reasonable? I have contacted them, and their offer seems a little too costly, as compared to self-planned bookings. Please suggest.

comments.author: @Distancebetweenbyshubh
comments.text:
A self-planned trip usually turns out cheaper, but you have to handle multiple bookings and plan the itinerary yourself. Lily’s services are good though, because I’ve taken packages from them twice. Even when the flight arrives early in the morning and the hotel doesn’t allow early check-in, they have a really nice office in Hanoi where you can freshen up.
The cost is higher mainly because they also have their profit margins. So, if you want more comfort and a smooth trip without the headache of managing different bookings, a package is a good option. Otherwise, if you feel you can make huge savings, you can definitely plan the trip on your own.

meta.title: 5 Things You Must Do in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon Travel Guide)
meta.description:
Ho Chi Minh City, still known to many as Saigon, is Vietnam’s largest and most dynamic city. In this video we explore five things you must do when visiting Ho Chi Minh City, from historic war sites to modern skyscrapers and one of the most famous nightlife streets in Southeast Asia.

Whether you are visiting for a few days or planning a longer trip through Vietnam, these must-do experiences will give you a great introduction to the culture, history, and energy of this incredible city. From the powerful exhibits inside the War Remnants Museum to the famous Ben Thanh Market, the skyline views from Bitexco Tower and Landmark 81, the lively nightlife of Bui Vien Walking Street, and the historic Cu Chi Tunnels just outside the city, these are some of the most memorable things to experience in Saigon.

If you're planning a trip to Vietnam, Ho Chi Minh City is a destination that blends history, modern development, and an unforgettable atmosphere.

meta.title: When Is the Best Time to Visit Hoi An Old Town? | Season + Time of Day Explained
meta.description:
When is the best time to visit Hoi An Old Town? The answer depends on more than just the weather.
In this guide, we break down the best time to visit Hoi An Old Town by season and time of day, so you can choose when to visit based on the kind of experience you want.
From February to April, Hoi An generally becomes milder and sunnier, making it comfortable for walking and exploring. May to July brings hotter weather, brighter days, more visitors, and higher accommodation demand around Da Nang's International Fireworks Festival.
August and September are a transition period, with the summer heat gradually easing while rain becomes more important. October and November are the wettest months, with a higher chance of heavy rain and flooding, although rainy season does not mean it rains all day, every day. December and January are generally drier and milder, although the weather can still be changeable.
The video also covers Tet, the Vietnamese Lunar New Year, when Hoi An becomes extremely busy and many businesses may close for several days at the beginning of the new year.
You'll also find a practical breakdown of the best times of day to explore Hoi An Old Town - from the quiet streets of early morning, to the most convenient sightseeing hours, changing afternoon light, and the lantern-filled atmosphere after dark.
In this video:

Urban versus rural access
While access to safe water is high in urban centers, this is not the case in rural areas, where most of Vietnam's population lives. 
Urban areas: In 2022, 75.8% of the urban population had access to safely managed drinking water.

meta.title: Hoi An Lantern Festival – Should You Go on Full Moon Night?
meta.description:
Should you go to the Hoi An Lantern Festival on full moon night?
It depends on the kind of experience you're looking for.
The Hoi An Lantern Festival is one of the most beautiful and iconic experiences in Vietnam. Every month, on the 14th day of the lunar calendar, lanterns illuminate the ancient town while parts of the public street lighting are dimmed, creating the warm atmosphere that has made Hoi An famous around the world.
But full-moon night is also the busiest time to visit.
In this video, Discover Da Nang shows you what the Hoi An Lantern Festival is really like during peak hours. We explore the busiest areas of the Ancient Town, including the Night Market, the Japanese Covered Bridge, and the Hoai River, where visitors line up for boat rides and floating lantern experiences.
Rather than simply recommending the festival, this video presents both sides of the experience. You'll see the beauty of thousands of glowing lanterns, but also the reality of large crowds, busy streets, and long queues that many first-time visitors don't expect.
You'll also learn practical tips before visiting, including:
• The best time to experience Hoi An at night
• Where the largest crowds usually gather
• What to expect from boat rides on the Hoai River
• How boat prices are typically arranged
• Tips for avoiding confusion before boarding
• A more environmentally responsible way to enjoy Hoi An's famous floating lantern tradition
If you prefer a quieter atmosphere, we also share some of the best alternatives - including weekday evenings, arriving before the peak crowds, staying later after most visitors leave, and exploring the peaceful streets just beyond the busiest tourist areas.
Whether you're planning your first trip to Hoi An or deciding if full-moon night is right for you, this video offers an honest, balanced look at one of Vietnam's most photographed destinations.
If you enjoy authentic travel guides with practical local advice, subscribe to Discover Da Nang for more videos about Da Nang, Hoi An, and Central Vietnam.

VIETNAM VISA FOR INDIANS (2026)
Mainland Vietnam (Hanoi · Da Nang · Ho Chi Minh) needs an e-visa: USD 25 single-entry / USD 50 multiple-entry, valid up to 90 days.

Apply ONLY on the official portal: https://evisa.xuatnhapcanh.gov.vn 
(processing 3–5 working days — apply 7–10 days ahead, passport valid 6+ months with 2 blank pages, carry a printed copy).

THE PHU QUOC VISA-FREE TRAP
Phu Quoc gives Indians a 30-day VISA-FREE stay — but ONLY if you fly in directly from abroad (via Bangkok / Kuala Lumpur) AND it is your only stop in Vietnam. The moment you transit Ho Chi Minh or Hanoi, that visa-free status is VOID and you need the e-visa. Doing a multi-city trip? Just get the e-visa — it's simpler and covers everything (a single-entry e-visa covers domestic flights inside Vietnam).

SKIP THE 2-HOUR IMMIGRATION QUEUE
Immigration can take up to 2 hours. A fast-track service meets you at the aerobridge, walks you through a priority lane, grabs your bags and loads your taxi — usually under 20 minutes. Book for your landing airport:

meta.title: The Hai Van Pass! Is It The Greatest Coastal Road In The World? #vietnam #topgear #travelvlog
meta.description:
Day 10 of our Vietnam Explorer Tour with TruTravels! Today we will show you the beautiful Hai Van Pass and let you see whether or not you think it deserves it’s reputation of, “Greatest Coastal Road In The World!”

Welcome back everyone! We are on day 10 of our Vietnam Adventure and you better believe this was a good day! 

In this video we will be leaving the beautiful lantern town of Hoi An and heading to our next destination, the city of Huế! 

To get to Huế, we travelled in style… open top Jeeps along the breathtaking coastal road, the Hai Van Pass. Before embarking on this journey, we had to say our fond farewells to two of the most amazing people we have ever had the pleasure of meeting, Harry and Miles. Without getting too sentimental, we just want to express our love for these guys and thank them for giving us so many hilarious and touching memories in the short time we spent with them. We can’t wait for a reunion! 

After a teary farewell, we headed off with our group, stopping off at the beach for some amazing food and get some instagramable snaps!

We won’t spoil too much of this part of the video in the description… so get watching!

Finally, when we arrived, our guide took us to the water where we were given the opportunity to watch the sunset on a private boat. 

Thank you for watching everyone. Feel free to subscribe, hit the like button and if you want to see more of our Vietnam posts, check out our Vietnam playlist and ring the bell to stay notified for when day 11 drops!

Love,

Jack and Lindsey! X

comments.text:
Big fat thumbs up for your family to take the time to stop by Hue.  I think Hue is the most underrated city in Vietnam.  It's a city with a very unique pace and atmosphere and feel.  If you want to get away from the hectic pace of HCMC and Ha Noi, Hue is the place.  Cultured, low key and quiet people, not resort staff friendly but the subtle niceness of an old historic city.

I used to live and work in VN and my Vietnamese friends told me the people in Hue have the softest accent but the people there is the most principled and disciplined people in all of Vietnam.  

Back in 2002, I stopped in Hue and caught the Hue Festival, by chance, see the two high schools on Le Loi Boulevard ending and got to see hundreds of Vietnamese female students walk out of the gate in their traditional "ao dai" flowing and they looked like butterflies streaming out.  Saw couple of teenage boys on bicycles picking up their girlfriend on their bicycles and felt like I was in a novel.  I got a peek inside those high school school yard and was blown away by how beautiful those 2 high schools were.
