meta.title: Da Nang's Best-Kept Secret? We Found a Michelin Seafood Spot & the Coziest Cafe in Vietnam
meta.description:
🦞 Da Nang has some of the freshest seafood in all of Vietnam — and I found a Michelin-listed spot hidden in a quiet alley that will blow your mind.

In this video, I take you to MOC Seafood (Mộc Quán), a legendary restaurant where the staff literally shell your seafood at the table, and then wind down at the dreamy Heaven Coffee with rooftop river views you won't forget.

📍 Heaven Coffee: 201 Chương Dương, Ngũ Hành Sơn, Da Nang

meta.title: Is Marble Mountains Worth It? Da Nang Vietnam
meta.description:
Is Marble Mountains worth it? We finally hiked Da Nang's most famous landmark in Vietnam after living here for 10 months — and the honest answer surprised us. Five hills named for the five elements, caves you can climb straight through, and the whole coast opening up at the top. Here's everything you need to know before you go.
Places Featured:

Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son), Da Nang
Gate A — the quiet back entrance
The grand cave with light falling through the ceiling
The tight cave you push through to reach the summit
The marble carving shops at the base

What We Cover:

Gate A vs. the tour-bus gate (and which to pick)
Ticket prices and the glass elevator option
The caves once used as wartime hospitals
The best time to go to beat the heat and crowds
What to bring so you're not caught out like we were

meta.title: Linh Ung Pagoda & The Giant Lady Buddha | Da Nang 2026
meta.channel: Adventurous Alex and Ukrainian Girl Olena
meta.description:
Visiting the Giant Lady Buddha at Linh Ung Pagoda | Da Nang, Vietnam 🇻🇳

In this video we visited Linh Ung Pagoda on Son Tra Peninsula in Da Nang, home to the famous 67-meter Lady Buddha statue, one of the most impressive landmarks in the city. The temple is beautifully maintained and offers amazing views over Da Nang, the coastline, and the surrounding mountains.

This is definitely one of the must-visit places in Da Nang, especially if you want a mix of culture, beautiful scenery, and one of the most iconic viewpoints in the city.

We got here by Grab from our hotel, Hilton Garden Inn Da Nang, and the ride cost us 104,000 VND, which was super easy and convenient.

📍 Address: Linh Ung Pagoda, Bai But, Son Tra Peninsula, Da Nang, Vietnam 
🕒 Hours: Daily, 6:00 AM – 6:00 PM 
🎟️ Admission: Free

If you’re planning a trip to Da Nang, I highly recommend adding this place to your itinerary.

Thank you so much for watching and traveling with us! ❤️ 
Don’t forget to like, subscribe, and check out our other Vietnam travel videos.

meta.title: 15 Things to Know BEFORE Visiting VIETNAM!
meta.description:
Vietnam is a country that surprises you at every turn — from the chaotic charm of Hanoi’s Old Quarter to the peaceful lantern‑lit nights of Hoi An, and the dramatic limestone cliffs of Cat Ba and Ha Long Bay.In this video, we share 15 essential things you need to know before visiting Vietnam, based on nearly three months of real travel experience across cities, small towns, and nature escapes.

You’ll learn:How to navigate Vietnam using Grab, trains, and sleeper buses.  Why cash and digital payments both matter.

The best times to visit and what to expect from Vietnam’s tropical weather.  How to experience the local culture — from street food stalls and coffee shops.  Insider tips for budget travel, language basics, and avoiding tourist traps. 

We’ll take you through our journey from Hanoi to Da Nang, stopping at Cat Ba, Hoi An, and other unforgettable spots — showing you what to pack, what to expect, and how to make the most of your time in Vietnam.  Whether you’re planning a short holiday or a long adventure, this guide will help you arrive prepared and travel confidently through one of Southeast Asia’s most captivating destinations.

meta.title: What Marble Mountains Is REALLY Like | Da Nang, Vietnam
meta.description:
We visited Marble Mountains also known as Ngu Hanh Son in Da Nang, Vietnam to see what it was really like.

We’d seen the beautiful photos, read the reviews and watched plenty of videos before coming here, so we had a pretty good idea of what to expect. But once we actually visited, our experience was a little different from what we had seen online.

We're not trying to say Marble Mountains isn't worth visiting. It’s a beautiful place and we’re glad we went. But we wanted to show you our honest experience so you can get a better idea of what it's really like and decide for yourself.

If you're planning a trip to Da Nang, Vietnam, or looking for things to do in Da Nang, hopefully this video gives you a better idea of what to expect when visiting Marble Mountains.

meta.title: Exploring the Hidden Gem of Vietnam: 3 Days in Cat Ba Island 🏝️🇻🇳
meta.description:
Today we explore the ABSOLUTELY beautiful island located in the north of Vietnam just a quick 2 hours from Hanoi, Cat Ba Island. We explore the beaches, Lan Ha Bay, and the food this island has to offer. This video is a more chilled and relaxed vlog because that is exactly how we felt on this island. 

Grab a cup of tea or your favorite beverage and enjoy this relaxed video. Thanks for tuning in once again and see you next time.

We met here in Bangkok, Thailand🇹🇭, fell in love, and finally eloped in March 2023. 💍💍(eeek!) Since 2021, we've been planning adventures, exploring South East Asia on motorbike, trying crazy fruits, and jungle trekking/hiking through some of the craziest places we've ever been. We want to bring you along on our journeys as we do our favorite things in South East Asia, which is HIKING and RIDING OUR MOTORBIKE in beautiful areas. (amongst many other activities haha) 

We hope our channel brings you inspiration in your travels and maybe a few laughs as well. We have a passion for being in the outdoors, capturing the special moments, and of course, sharing it with you.

meta.title: Lobster Sashimi Dang Nang Seafood Feast! Dao Xanh Quan
meta.description:
Da Nang is famous for live seafood. So many restaurants to choose from!
Our family first lobster sashimi experience was at Nha Hang Dao Xanh in Da Nang. For lunch we had the whole place to ourselves!
We ordered oysters for AU$5 each and a 600g lobster sashimi. Bigger lobster will be more meatier. Not much flesh in a 600g lobster.
The prawns were my favourite! Super sweet and fleshy - just how I like it!
GeoDuck was also something not common in Sydney so I had to order but a bigger one to what we ordered would have given us more to eat.
We live to learn 
The seafood fried rice was the stomach filler but for only AU$6 it was definitely a bargain!
Can never go wrong with morning glory in asia. Cheap and delicious
It was good to try as the price was better than some on My Khe Beach but I do prefer Be Man Restaurant for the location, variety and price. Check out my previous video for my review of Be Man.

meta.title: Our Vietnam Travel Guide 2024 | First time in HANOI, HOI AN, & HO CHI MINH
meta.description:
In today's video we visit the amazingly beautiful country of Vietnam and provide travel tips and tricks to make your visit better. Vietnam is a beautiful and culturally rich country that has become a popular destination for travelers from all over the world and 2024 is a great time to visit.

Hanoi, the capital city, is known for its bustling streets, French colonial architecture, and delicious street food. Some of the top attractions in Hanoi include the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the Temple of Literature, and the Old Quarter.

Hoi An, located in central Vietnam, is a picturesque city known for its well-preserved Ancient Town, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The town features charming streets lined with historic buildings, temples, and colorful lanterns. Hoi An is also famous for its tailor shops, where visitors can have custom-made clothing and accessories created for them. We visited Hoi An especially for the amazing lantern festival, which is held each month during the full moon.

Ho Chi Minh City, formerly known as Saigon, is the largest city in Vietnam and is located in the southern part of the country. The city is a vibrant hub of culture and commerce, with numerous markets, museums, and historical sites to explore. Some of the top attractions in Ho Chi Minh City include the War Remnants Museum, the Cu Chi Tunnels, and the Notre-Dame Cathedral.

Traveling from Hanoi to Hoi An and then down to Ho Chi Minh City allows visitors to experience a diverse range of cultural and historical attractions, as well as stunning landscapes and delicious cuisine. The journey between these cities can be made by plane, train, bus, or private car, and there are numerous tour companies and travel agencies that can help plan and organize a trip. We took Vietnam Airlines between locations and everything turned out great.

Read the blogs on our website:

Video # 110

▶️ We started our channel to inspire and share our world travel lifestyle, adventures, and optimistic outlook on life with others. After completing a two-year journey in our Airstream to see all 50 states and 51 National Parks, we left to travel abroad. We have downsized our possessions and sold our home so that we can wander about with only the things in our backpacks. 

We love living on the road, traveling each week to a new location. We plan to travel extensively to every part of the world. Ours is not a slow travel lifestyle but rather a vagabondish one. The goal is not to check a country off a list, but to experience it by meeting new people, seeing how others live, and making new friends. We believe in laughing, loving, and living our lives to the fullest. 

We are working hard to build a beautiful website where you can get travel information about the places we have been. In addition, we post blog articles to help you travel better. Our channel is a way of augmenting that effort, so sometimes we post videos about how to travel or a vlog showing our lives on the road as we do an activity or an adventure. We also post Shorts, so check those out, too. We hope to entertain you, but most importantly, we want to inspire you and give you the confidence to plan your own adventure around the world. 

We invite you to subscribe and comment. We also hope you follow the link to our website and sign up for our newsletter. It's a great way to keep up-to-date with our travels. ◀️

transcript: A country where you find almost every  experience that you must have thought  of at some point in your travel bucket  list. On one side, mountains nestled  above the clouds and the world's  largest caves. And on the other,  crystal-clear beaches. World-famous  Vietnamese coffee, Asia's craziest  nightlife, the world's longest cable  car, or French-style cities, or the raw  history of the Vietnam War; there is so  much variety in this one country that  every day feels like you've arrived in  a new land. Welcome to Vietnam. Vietnam  is an S-shaped country located in  Southeast Asia that shares borders with  China, Laos, and Cambodia. It stretches  for about 1,650 km from North to South.  That is why, in a single trip, you get  to see cold mountains, tropical beaches , modern cities, and centuries-old  culture, all of it. Hey guys, this is  Shashank and welcome back to my channel . I hope you are doing absolutely good.  So, right now I am in Vietnam and I am  going to share a complete itinerary for  Vietnam that will be for 7, 8, or 9  days. In which we will visit Hanoi, Da  Nang, and travel everywhere, and in  this video, I will tell you how you can  come here. Which cheap flight you  should take. Where should you get your  visa from? How much will it cost? Where  can you stay? Where can you do shopping ? Where will you eat Indian food? I am  going to tell you everything in detail.  For children, pregnant women, and  senior citizens, what it's like, how  much you have to walk, I will talk  about everything in detail. And in the  end, I will also give you a budget  summary. So let's start our Vietnam  trip. Come with me. Now let's talk  about the best time to visit. Vietnam's  weather varies quite a bit between the  North, Central, and South regions.  Therefore, it is better to choose the  season according to the destination.  For North Vietnam, including Hanoi, Ha  Long Bay, Ninh Binh, and Sapa, October  to December is the best. For Central  Vietnam, including Da Nang, Hoi An, and  Hue, February to August is the best.  For South Vietnam, including Ho Chi  Minh City and Phu Quoc, November to  April is the best. And if you want to  cover the entire Vietnam, then the  period between October and April is  overall the most convenient and  comfortable. During this period,  exploring multiple regions in a single  trip is comparatively easier. This trip  has been planned through a company  called Way For Travel. So, if you want  their details, you can see them on the  side of the screen, and I will also put  them in the description below, and if  you are looking for a trusted partner,  you can consider them. So, first, let's  talk about how to reach. Traveling to  Vietnam from India is quite easy. From  Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Ahmedabad.  Direct flights to Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh  are available. There are three major  international airports in Vietnam.  Hanoi in the North, Da Nang in the  Center, and Ho Chi Minh in the South.  If you book flights two to three months  in advance, return flights can be found  for around 20,000 to 25,000. I booked  my return flight for 22,000, which also  included 15 kg of extra baggage. If you  want to travel on a budget, VietJet Air  is the most affordable option, and if  budget is not an issue, Vietnam  Airlines is the best option. If you  want to know how you can find the  cheapest flights, just type "flights"  in the comments. Now let's talk about  visa and travel insurance. It is  mandatory for Indians to get an e-visa  to travel to Vietnam, and the good  thing is that the process is quite  simple. Indian passport holders can  apply for a single-entry or  multiple-entry visa. Which can be valid  for a maximum of 90 days. And keep in  mind that visa-on-arrival is not  available for Indians in Vietnam.  Therefore, it is necessary to get an  e-visa before the trip. You can apply  for an e-visa online through the  official Vietnam Immigration website.  For the application, you mainly need to  fill in passport details, a  passport-sized photo, entry/exit dates,  and some basic information. If you need  any help related to the visa, please  comment "visa". I will share a proper  guide with you. Normally, the visa  processing can take around three  working days. But do not take the risk  of waiting until the last moment. I  would recommend that you apply for the  visa at least two weeks before your  trip. And one very important tip: apply  for the visa only through the official  government website. I will put the link  to the official e-visa website in the  description. After visa approval,  definitely carry a printout with your  passport because you might need it  during immigration. Now let's talk  about travel insurance. Travel  insurance is not mandatory for Vietnam.  But I personally would strongly  recommend it. Usually, basic insurance  costs around ₹ 300 to ₹ 800, which  is very useful in unexpected situations  like medical emergencies, baggage loss,  flight-related issues, or trip  cancellations. Now let's talk about SIM  cards and money exchange because a  little smart planning here can save you  a lot of money. Vietnamese Dong is used  for daily transactions in Vietnam.  Before exchanging currency, definitely  check the current exchange rate on the  screen. If you prefer to carry cash, it  is better to take USD. Instead of  purchasing Vietnamese Dong directly  from India, carry USD. Do not exchange  all your money at the airport. Only  exchange $ 50 so that you can manage a  taxi, bus, or basic expenses from the  airport to your hotel. Instead of  exchanging money at just one shop in  the city, compare rates at three or  four places. Besides cash, you can also  use forex cards, international debit or  credit cards, or neo-cards. ATMs are  easily available in tourist areas of  Vietnam, and cards are also accepted at  major restaurants, malls, and shopping  centers. Still, keep some cash handy  for emergencies. There are some UPI  apps that you can use in Vietnam. Write  "app" in the comments and I will share  its name. Now let's talk about SIM  cards. There is no need to buy a SIM  card directly from the airport because  prices can be higher. You can get a  local SIM from a Viettel official store , pre-book via Klook to pick it up at  the airport, or get an eSIM from Agoda.  You will easily find a SIM online for  400 to 500 rupees. Now let's talk about  stay options. In Vietnam, you can find  stay options for every budget. Just try  to book a hotel in the city center area  so that sightseeing, cafes, and markets  are easily accessible. Hostels are a  very affordable option for budget  travelers. Where you can get dorm beds  for 500 to 800 rupees per day. If you  prefer hotels, you can easily find  clean and comfortable double occupancy  rooms for 1500 to 3000 rupees per night . And if you need a little extra space  or a kitchen, Airbnb is a good option.  You can find fully furnished apartments  for 2000 to 3000 per night. If you want  a list of the best Airbnbs, comment " Airbnb". I will share the complete PDF.  So let's start with our Day One. Most  flights from India to Hanoi are late at  night and land between 5:00 and 7:00 AM . After immigration and baggage, you  should be out of the airport by around  8:00 AM. Freshen up at the airport,  connect to the free Wi-Fi, and exchange  around $ 50 into Dong for initial  expenses. Do not take a SIM from the  airport because prices here are three  to four times higher. After dropping  your luggage at the hotel, first head  to St. Joseph's Cathedral, whose  French-style architecture will give you  a Euro-vibe feel. From there, walk to  Hoan Kiem Lake and explore Ngoc Son  Temple. After that, definitely try the  famous egg coffee or coconut coffee at  The Note Cafe. After lunch, check into  your hotel and rest for two to three  hours. Make sure to go watch a water  puppet show in the evening. Where you  can experience Vietnam's culture and  traditions in an interesting way. Now  let's talk about local transportation.  In Vietnam, you get options like  self-drive bikes, Grab cars like Ola/ Uber, Grab bikes like Rapido, and local  buses. The most budget-friendly option  is a self-drive scooter, which costs  around 400 to 500 rupees per day. Local  buses charge 40 to 50 rupees, or Grab  bikes charge 100 to 150 rupees per trip . Grab taxis charge a bit more, but  they fit the budget. If you are  traveling with three to four people.  Exploring Da Nang by scooter is quite  easy and convenient. But there is a  common confusion here. Is an Indian  driving license valid in Vietnam? It is  mandatory to obtain an International  Driving Permit. Which is used along  with your Indian driving license. If  you also want to apply for an IDP,  comment "IDP" below. I will share the  link with you. Hey guys, very good  morning. Today we are going to Ha Long  Bay, and our bus has arrived. Let's go  and see how it goes. Hotel pickup  generally happens between 7:00 AM and  8:00 AM. Ha Long Bay is a UNESCO World  Heritage site. After an approximately 2 -hour drive from Hanoi, you reach Ha  Long Bay. There are basically two  cruise options here. One is a day  cruise, and the other is a two-day,  one-night cruise. On a day cruise, you  get activities like lunch, kayaking,  and cave exploration. The night cruise  has almost the same activities. But the  experience is a bit more relaxed and  luxurious. Because you stay overnight  on the cruise itself. However, the  price of a night cruise is almost 3x  more expensive than a day cruise. On a  day cruise, you first explore the Sung  Sot Cave. Where you get to see  beautiful rock formations with colorful  lights. After that, there will be a  bamboo boat ride or kayaking, which is  included, where you can enjoy limestone  caves and amazing natural views up  close. And then there is a stop at Ti  Top Island. Where you can swim and also  explore the island. After the cruise,  you will return to Hanoi in the evening . You are dropped off at your hotel by  8:00 PM. After freshening up at the  hotel, you can head out to explore  Train Street. Now let's talk about  language and local behavior. The  official language of Vietnam is  Vietnamese, and very few people know  English. So, be sure to download Google  Translate before your trip, as the  locals 'behavior and communication  style might be a bit different. So,  avoid unnecessary arguments. Deal with  things politely and just enjoy the trip . Keep day three for Ninh Binh. Now,  day three is optional. If you want to  go to Ninh Binh, you can. Otherwise, as  an option, you can also fly to Da Nang.  People also know Ninh Binh as the Ha  Long Bay on land. This is a full-day  tour. Departure from Hanoi to Ninh Binh  will be in the morning. Here, you first  get to experience the Tam Coc boat ride . Where local women row the boats with  their feet. It is quite a unique  experience. After this, you visit the  Hoa Lu ancient capital and explore  temples connected to Vietnam's ancient  emperors. If you like adventure, climb  the 500 steps of Mua Caves and enjoy  the amazing panoramic view of Ninh Binh  from the top. After completing the tour  in the evening, you get dropped off at  your hotel in Hanoi around 8:00 PM.  After freshening up, you can explore  Beer Street and do some shopping. Now  let's talk about food options. If you  are a non-vegetarian, then Vietnam is a  food paradise for you. Here you will  easily find seafood, chicken, pork,  beef, mutton, and many local dishes,  and that too on a very low budget. And  if you prefer vegetarian or Jain food,  then there is no need to worry at all.  You can find Indian restaurants in  every major city. Veg and Jain food  options are available there. Indian  food is a bit expensive. Like, for two  people, you will have to spend around  1000 to 1500 rupees. If you are staying  in an Airbnb, you can take basic  cooking essentials from India and cook  for yourself. If you want a list of veg  or Jain restaurants or an Airbnb guide,  write "Veg" or "Airbnb" in the comments . I will share all the details with you  in a PDF. Day four, today you have to  leave Hanoi for Da Nang. You can choose  a flight, train, or bus according to  your budget and convenience. Da Nang is  a beautiful coastal city in Vietnam.  After reaching the hotel, checking in,  and freshening up, head straight to  explore the Marble Mountains. Where you  get to see caves, temples, and amazing  viewpoints. Book your tickets in  advance. Because I took this package  from Way For Travel. So, all the  tickets and tours were already booked  by Way For Travel. My Khe Beach is  perfect to relax in the evening. Take a  walk on the beach. Enjoy the sunset and  just chill. Head to Dragon Bridge at  night. If it's the weekend, don't miss  the Fire and Water show here. For  dinner, you can try local Vietnamese  food. And if you want Indian food, you  can easily find Indian restaurants. Now  let's talk about senior citizens,  pregnant women, and kids. Vietnam is a  family-friendly destination, and with a  little planning, your trip can be very  comfortable. For senior citizens, the  Vietnam experience can be quite  comfortable. Just keep the itinerary  relaxed and use cabs to explore the  city. Places like Hoi An, Ba Na Hills,  Marble Mountains, Ninh Binh, and Ha  Long Bay caves involve some walking and  stairs in places. So wear comfortable  shoes and make sure to take breaks in  between. If you want a senior  citizen-friendly Vietnam itinerary,  write "Senior Citizen" in the comments.  I will share it with you. Now, talking  about kids, Vietnam is an amazing  destination for them. Theme parks,  cable cars, beaches, boat rides,  aquariums, and cultural shows. They are  going to enjoy it a lot. Just pay extra  attention to children in crowded areas  and when crossing roads, and always  wear life jackets during boat rides or  any water activities. Now, for pregnant  women, keep the itinerary a bit relaxed . Avoid unnecessary long travel and  enjoy the trip by staying in each city  for two to three days. Day five, Ba Na  Hills. Dedicate the entire day to  exploring Ba Na Hills. Where the most  famous attraction is the Golden Bridge.  Where you can see the mountain view  between the giant hands. Try to take  the 8:00 AM cable car because the crowd  is comparatively less early in the  morning and you can take comfortable  photos and videos. Definitely carry a  warm jacket because the weather on top  of Ba Na Hills is much colder compared  to Da Nang. After the Golden Bridge,  explore the French Village and Fantasy  Park. You will find many beautiful  photo spots here. If you want a  complete guide on what to explore in Ba  Na Hills, comment "Ba Na Hills." I will  share a proper PDF with you. After  enjoying the whole day at Ba Na Hills,  return to Da Nang in the evening, and  if you have time and energy left at  night, do explore the Da Nang night  market. Now let's talk about important  things to carry. Before starting the  trip, make sure to pack these things.  You can see the complete packing  checklist on the screen, and it will  also be in the description. If you want  this entire guide in PDF form, then  comment "Checklist" and I will share it . On Day Six, start your morning by  visiting Lady Buddha, a famous  attraction in Da Nang. From there, you  get a beautiful view of the sea and the  city. After lunch, Hoi An is just a 45- minute drive from Da Nang. You can also  easily reach there by renting a scooter  for around ₹ 400. Hoi An is a  beautiful ancient town. The yellow  buildings and colorful lanterns make  the entire town look very vibrant.  First, enjoy a coconut boat ride in Cam  Thanh Village and experience the  traditional Vietnamese boat dance, then  explore the Japanese Covered Bridge and  the local market where you can also buy  souvenirs. And as evening falls, make  sure to take a lantern boat ride on the  Thu Bon River. At night, the entire Hoi  An town looks so beautiful with  colorful lanterns that this experience  simply cannot be missed. Now, let's  talk about shopping options. There are  plenty of shopping options available  for both men and women in Vietnam, and  prices are quite affordable. There are  many international brand factories here , so you can find branded products and  apparel for very cheap. Just make sure  to bargain, as shopkeepers will  initially quote you three to four times  the price. If you need any help related  to shopping, comment "shopping". I will  share the complete PDF. Day Seven.  Today's next stop will be Ho Chi Minh  City. To reach here from Da Nang, you  have three options: flight, bus, or  train. Upon reaching the city, check  into your hotel. Freshen up. After that , head out to the Saigon Central Post  Office for sightseeing. If you want to  cover maximum places in less time, the  Hop-on Hop-off bus is the best option,  covering the city's major attractions  in about two hours. After this, visit  the War Remnants Museum, where you will  get a chance to understand the history  of the Vietnam War and its impact. In  the evening, sit at a rooftop café to  enjoy the beautiful skyline and sunset  of Ho Chi Minh City. Now, let's talk  about important apps. Before going to  Vietnam, make sure to install these  apps, as they will be very useful  during your trip. Reserve the last day  of Vietnam for the Cu Chi Tunnels and  the Mekong Delta. Go to explore the Cu  Chi Tunnels in the morning. Where you  can see how soldiers used underground  tunnels during the Vietnam War. After  lunch, head out for the Mekong Delta.  Where along with a boat ride, you get a  chance to explore traditional villages,  coconut factories, and rice paper  workshops. In the evening, return to Ho  Chi Minh City, rest for a while, and  then head to the airport for your  return flight. Now, let's talk about  drone rules. If you are taking a drone  to Vietnam, keep one important thing in  mind. To fly a drone here, you need  prior approval permission from the  Ministry of National Defence, and  foreign travelers also need a local  sponsor for the permit. If you want the  complete process on how to legally fly  a drone in Vietnam and how to get  permission, DM me "DRONE" on Instagram.  Now talking about the budget, you can  get a return flight from India to  Vietnam for ₹ 25,000 to ₹ 30,000.  Decent stay options are available for  ₹ 2,000 to ₹ 4,000 per day. For 7  days, it will cost around ₹ 18,000 to  ₹ 25,000. Food is quite affordable.  If you eat non-veg and can have street  food, it costs about ₹ 300 to ₹ 500  per day. But day tours, travel, and  sightseeing increase the budget  significantly. So, if you want a  hassle-free option instead of planning  it yourself, you can also consider a  package of ₹ 20,000 per person  excluding flights. Which includes stay,  transfers, and sightseeing, everything.  Now let's talk about the itinerary. If  you have 10 days, you can include Sapa  in your itinerary. If you have 13 days,  definitely include Phu Quoc, and if you  are coming for 15 days, you can  comfortably cover both Sapa and Phu  Quoc. meta.title: Vietnam’s Most Dangerous Mountain Road, The Hai Van Pass
meta.description:
Week 21 in Da Nang. We'd had our motorbike for exactly two days when we decided to ride it up and over the Hai Van Pass. One of the most iconic mountain roads in Southeast Asia.

Friends visiting from the UK were driving up to Hue, we joined them for the ride over, stopped at a cafe on the way up, had seafood lunch at Lang Co beach, then turned around and rode home alone through the fog.

Got a little damp. Made it back before dark. 10/10 would do again. Genuinely one of the coolest days we've had in Vietnam.

If you're planning to do the Hai Van Pass — do it. Details below.

meta.title: Vietnam Travel Guide 2026 for Indians | Visa, Best Time, 9-Day Plan
meta.description:
Planning a Vietnam trip from India in 2026? This 10-minute guide covers everything: the best time to visit, how to get the Vietnam e-visa, where to go (Hanoi, Ha Long Bay, Ninh Binh, Sapa, Hoi An, Da Nang, Phong Nha, Saigon, Mekong Delta, Phu Quoc), where to stay, what to eat, how to get around, money and SIM tips, a simple 9-day itinerary and the 3 mistakes most first-timers make.

Want us to plan it? WhatsApp Trust and Trip and type VIETNAM: https://wa.me/918115999588?text=VIETNAM
Website: https://trustandtrip.com

QUICK ANSWERS
- Do Indians need a visa for Vietnam? Yes. Apply online for the Vietnam e-visa, only on the official government portal (evisa.gov.vn). Apply at least 2 weeks before you fly.
- Best time to visit Vietnam? It depends on the region. North (Hanoi, Ha Long): Oct-Apr. Centre (Hoi An, Da Nang): Feb-Aug. South (Saigon, Phu Quoc): Dec-Apr.
- How many days for Vietnam? 9 days covers Hanoi, Ha Long Bay, Hoi An and Saigon without rushing.
- How far is Vietnam from India? Direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata take about 4-6 hours.

meta.title: Hue Vietnam 4K | Explore the Imperial City, Royal Tombs & Hương River
meta.description:
Huế, Vietnam 4K — take a quiet journey through Vietnam’s former imperial capital, where ancient architecture, peaceful landscapes and the gentle Hương River create one of the country’s most atmospheric destinations.

This visual journey through Huế, Vietnam invites you to experience the city without narration — only beautiful scenery, gentle music and the quiet atmosphere of each place.

Travel through the historic Imperial City of Huế, admire the restored beauty of Kiến Trung Palace, and wander among the royal landscapes of Minh Mạng Mausoleum and Khải Định Mausoleum. Follow the Hương River past Thiên Mụ Pagoda and Trường Tiền Bridge, then discover the colors of Thủy Xuân Incense Village and the peaceful natural scenery surrounding Huế.

Once the imperial capital of the Nguyễn Dynasty, Huế, Vietnam is a place where architecture, history, nature and a slower rhythm of life still exist side by side.

There is no story to follow in this film and nothing you need to understand.
Just slow down, listen, and spend a little time in Huế.

This is Stepping into Stillness — a visual journey from Stepping into Wonder, created for moments when a place needs fewer words and more room to simply be experienced.

Featured places:
Huế Imperial City • Kiến Trung Palace • Minh Mạng Mausoleum • Khải Định Mausoleum • Thiên Mụ Pagoda • Hương River • Trường Tiền Bridge • Thủy Xuân Incense Village • Lăng Cô

Until our next journey, keep wondering.

#HueVietnam #Vietnam4K #HueImperialCity #VietnamTravel #SteppingIntoWonder

comments.text: Sujith Bro, Ho Chi Minh City is very famous for street food. But you should very careful in selecting food items. Shell fish is most dangerous food stuff if not properly cooked. Vietnam is a developing country and snooty traffic is famous as you could see in all major traffic areas. You could see the reminents of Vietnam war, while southern Vietnam is supported by USA while northern area was controlled by Russian army. Happy travel, bro!

Hi Sujith, the Vietnamese leader Ho Chi Minh's body is on display in this mausoleum & historic site in Hanoi. Please try not to miss it when you are in Hanoi. There's strict rules before entering to meet the legendary "Uncle Ho".

Hanoi is an administrative city and is a very subdued city as compared with HCM city, which is more hot and happening.

Happy to see HCM city (bikes city) thru your lens and maybe later of Hanoi, the 2 Vietnamese cities I last visited 2 months ago. 

Being a heavily populated bike city, please be careful with your phone/camera while shooting from city pavements.  I am always closely guarded by my local staff when I am walking on the pavements and roadside.

Greetings from 🇲🇾  🇲🇾

meta.title: 3 Days in Da Nang Vietnam 🇻🇳 Best Cafes, Food & Beachfront Hotel | Vietnam Travel Guide 2026
meta.description:
Planning 3 days in Da Nang, Vietnam? 🇻🇳 In this travel vlog, we explore all the best things to do in Da Nang, one of Southeast Asia’s most underrated beach destinations.

Our 3 day itinerary through Central Vietnam starts with a stay at a luxury beachfront hotel with a stunning view of both Da Nang's famous coastline and its lush mountains. From there, we discover the city's vibrant food scene through its best cafes and Michelin-awarded restaurants loved by locals. From a beloved grandmother's banh mi shop to a popular egg coffee spot to a Masterchef owned fish noodle shop, you'll never run out of amazing food in this seaside city.

Whether you’re visiting Vietnam for the first time or planning your next Southeast Asia trip, this Da Nang Vietnam travel vlog will help you discover all the best Vietnamese food, coffee shops and places to visit on your next trip.

comments.text:
Thank you for the incredible video, Ralph & Sam. It’s an honor to have our family’s story shared on your channel.

What we do today in Da Nang traces back to my grandmother, who began this craft in 1968. Her methods and discipline live on through my mother and me. 

Our goal has always been simple: protect that tradition and share it with others. As a new Da Nang shop, your support and visibility help us do exactly that and give us every reason to keep going. Thank you.

meta.title: How to Visit Hoi An from Da Nang: Full Travel Guide
meta.description:
How to Visit Hoi An from Da Nang | Complete Travel Guide

Hoi An is just 30km south of Da Nang — around 45 minutes to 1 hour by car. You can take a taxi, book a Grab, ride a shuttle, or take the Yellow Public Bus (cheapest option, but less comfortable).

Many travelers visit Hoi An as a day trip, but staying at least one night is recommended to fully enjoy the atmosphere, food, and lantern-lit streets.

Top Things to Know:

Historical Significance: Hoi An was a major Southeast Asian trading port from the 15th to 19th century. Merchants from China, Japan, and Europe left behind a unique mix of architecture.

UNESCO World Heritage Site: The ancient town is exceptionally well preserved.

Lantern Festival: Held monthly during the full moon. Electric lights are turned off, and the streets glow with lanterns and candles on the river.

Tailor Shops: Over 400 shops offer custom suits, dresses, shoes, and bags — often completed within 1–2 days.

Night Market: Starts around 5 PM across the river. Expect street food, souvenirs, and colorful lanterns.

Local Food to Try:

Cao Lau – chewy noodles with pork, herbs, and croutons
White Rose Dumplings
Hoi An Banh Mi
Cooking Classes: Includes market tours and hands-on instruction.

Travel Tips:

Ask for Grab driver prices upfront to avoid detours or upselling.
Avoid common upsells at tailor shops and souvenir stores.
Morning visits offer fewer crowds and better photo opportunities.
Keep an eye on your belongings at the night market.

This guide gives you everything you need to visit Hoi An with confidence and make the most of your time there.

meta.description:
How to Plan a Day Trip to Hoi An from Da Nang (2026 Guide) | Da Nang to Hoi an tour | hoi an vietnam | lady buddha da nang | marble mountain da nang vietnam | da nang to hoi an day trip | da nang to hoi an travel | da nang hoi an trip

Are you planning a Da Nang to Hoi An day trip in 2026? In this Vietnam travel vlog, I’m taking you on an epic half-day group tour to show you exactly how to plan your itinerary and what to expect along the way!

We kick off the day at the Son Tra Peninsula to see the spectacular Lady Buddha Da Nang—the tallest Buddha statue in Vietnam—before heading to the epic Marble Mountains. I'll show you what it's really like to explore the ancient cave temples, pagodas, and the traditional stone carving village. Finally, we end the tour wandering through the magical, lantern-lit streets of Hoi An Ancient Town.

Whether you are wondering how to get from Da Nang to Hoi An, if a guided half-day tour is worth the money, or how many stairs are actually at the Marble Mountains, this complete 2026 travel guide has everything you need to know.

One of the best meal I ever had was in a dirty Central Highlands city called Kontum.  At about 5am, I pulled my motorbike over and bought a sandwich from an early-opening stand.  The vender’s English was as negligible as my Vietnamese so I just pointed to one of the sandwiches already made.
It was really delicious: creamy and rich and oddly sweet — and tantalizingly familiar.  After a few bites, I cracked it open: the filling was... granulated sugar and butter.
Now, I cannot recommend this dish as an actual food, but at that moment, jet-lagged, sleep-deprived, isolated, my body needed exactly that.

meta.description:
Join us as we explore the vibrant culinary scene of Hoi An, Vietnam, by taking part in an authentic Vietnamese cooking class. In this video, we dive into the heart of local food culture, Hands-on cooking lessons led by a local chef. From traditional dishes like Cao Lau and Papaya Salad to learning unique cooking techniques, this experience offers a delicious insight into Vietnamese cuisine. Perfect for fellow travel enthusiasts, food lovers, or anyone planning a trip to Vietnam, this video showcases why a cooking class in Hoi An is a must-do cultural activity. Subscribe for more travel adventures as we continue exploring the world one unforgettable experience at a time.

▶ Tik Tok - BangAverage_travel

🚨 MENU AND INGREDIENTS 🚨

    Crispy Vietnamese Pancake:
 Ingredients:
 • White rice powder (50g)
 • Water (100ml)
 • Turmeric powder (0.05g)
 • Spring onion (0.05g)
 • Mushroom (10g)
 • Oil
 • Bean sprout
 • Soysauce for dipping
 • Preparation:
 • Mix water, rice powder, turmeric, and spring onion in a large bowl for 5 minutes.
 • Prepare a small bowl of mushroom.
 • Heat a pan and pour some oil.
 • Pour 4 soup spoons of rice powder milk onto the pan.
 • Place some bean sprout, mushroom, and cover for 3 minutes.
 • Serve on a plate with fresh vegetables and soy sauce for dipping.
 Banana Flower Salad:
       Ingredients:
 • Banana flower (0.2kg)
 • Papaya (0.2kg)
 • Boiled bird egg (2)
 • Tofu (0.1kg)
 • Onion (0.05kg)
 • Pepper mint (0.03kg)
 • Dry peanut bean (0.01kg)
 • Sweet and sour fish sauce for mixing salad:
 • Chilli sauce (1 coffee spoon)
 • Lime juice (1 coffee spoon)
 • Fish sauce (2 coffee spoons)
 • Sugar (1 coffee spoon)
 • Method:
 • Heat a pan and stir-fry tofu, black pepper, sugar for 3 minutes.
 • Wait for it to cool.
 • Mix salad with banana flower, papaya, onions, mint, and sauce.
 • Serve on a plate and decorate with sesame, peanut, and boiled egg.
 Grilled Eggplant on Charcoal with Peanut Sauce:
 Ingredients:
 • Peanut sauce:
 • Onion (0.02kg)
 • Shallot (0.02kg)
 • Ginger (0.02kg)
 • Dry peanut (0.02kg)
 • Method:
 • Chop onion, shallot, ginger, and grind dry peanut.
 • Heat a pan and cook the peanut sauce.
 • Grill eggplant on charcoal.
 • Serve with peanut sauce.
 • Heat the pan and add some cooking oil.
 • Pour the marinated vegetables (soya sauce, fish sauce, sugar, black pepper, dry peanut, chilli sauce) into the pan.
 • Cook until the vegetables are fragrant.
 • Pour the mixture into a small bowl.
 • This recipe serves 2 people.
 • Grill the eggplant until well done.
 • Peel the skin and cut the eggplant into small pieces.
 • Take one soup spoon of peanut sauce and pour it over the eggplant.
 • Decorate the plate with the eggplant.
 • Buy fresh rice noodle paper or dry rice paper and dip it in warm water.
 • Take one small spoon of peanut sauce and put it on the rice paper.
 • Roll the rice paper and cut it in half.
 • Decorate the plate with the rice paper.
 Chicken Cao Lau:
 Ingredients:
 • Chicken breast slice: 0.3kg
 • Spring onion chop: 0.01kg
 • Chilli sauce: 1 chilli spoon
 • Soya sauce
 • Cao lau noodle: 0.5kg
 • Bean Sprout: 0.3kg
 • Method:
 • Heat the pan and add some cooking oil.
 • Pour the chicken into the pan and cook for 5 minutes.
 • Stir-fry the Cao lau noodle and try until it’s cooked.
 • Add chilli sauce, sugar, soy sauce, and stir-fry everything together with the spring onion.
 • Pour the mixture into a bowl and decorate with black pepper.
 Caramel Banana:
 • Heat the pan until it’s really hot.
 • Pour some sugar into the pan.
 • Put the fresh banana on the pan.
 • Cook for 2 minutes, then turn the banana over.
 • Pick up the plate and serve.

meta.title: Exploring Son Tra Peninsula & Linh Ung Pagoda | Lady Buddha & Beautiful Views 🇻🇳 Vietnam Trip Day 2
meta.description:
Day 2 of our Vietnam family adventure takes us to the breathtaking Son Tra Peninsula in Da Nang! 🇻🇳🌿

The journey itself was already an experience as we traveled along the beautiful mountain roads, surrounded by lush greenery and amazing views of the coastline. 🌊⛰️

When we arrived at Linh Ung Pagoda, we were greeted by the magnificent Lady Buddha, standing peacefully above the sea and watching over Da Nang. 🙏✨

We explored the beautiful temple grounds, admired the traditional architecture, walked through the peaceful garden, and took in the incredible scenery all around us. 🌿🏯

There was something special about simply slowing down, looking around, and appreciating the beauty of this place.

From the winding road up Son Tra to the peaceful gardens and breathtaking views, every moment gave us another reason to stop and appreciate God's wonderful creation. ❤️

This was one of those places where the journey and the destination were both unforgettable. 🇻🇳✨

Come along with us as we experience Son Tra Peninsula and Linh Ung Pagoda, Da Nang, Vietnam!

Hoi An is one of Vietnam's most popular destinations. In this video, I'm going to share the best areas to stay near Hoi An's Old Town. 

First-time visitors to Hoi An and travelers looking for convenience - I recommend staying near the Old Town. Since it's a UNESCO Heritage Site, there are no hotels in this protected zone but there are many hotels near the town, within 10-minutes walking distance. There are many shops, restaurants, cafes, and of course the historical ancient houses and buildings in this town. This area is a no car-zone so there are only scooters and bicycles allowed which makes it pedestrian friendly.

meta.title: Honest Review of Marble Mountains & Shopping in Da Nang | Complete Travel Guide 2026
meta.description:
Is the Marble Mountain tour worth the climb? Today, we’re exploring one of Da Nang’s most iconic landmarks! 🇻🇳 We tackle the "Stairs vs. Lift" debate first-hand and share our honest review of the entire experience, from ancient caves to cheap shopping.

Day 7 of our Vietnam Series: We headed to the famous Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son), which are split into two main attractions: the mystical caves (including Am Phu Cave and Huyen Khong Cave) and the summit of Water Mountain.

In this vlog:

The Ultimate "Stairs vs. Lift" Challenge: We took separate paths to the summit to give you a complete perspective! Dilpreet opted for the convenience of the lift, while I challenged myself with the steep stone staircase to the top. We compare the views, the effort, and whether the climb is truly worth it.

Marble Mountain Caves: Exploring the dramatic, sun-dappled interior of the main caves.

Zumba on the Beach: Catching the local energy at Da Nang Beach with some sunset open-air Zumba.

Han Market Dash: We raced against the clock to reach Han Market just 15 minutes before its 7:00 PM closing!

Shopping Secret: We visited Vincom Plaza and discovered that VinMart is nearly 30% cheaper than other tourist shops in Da Nang for essentials and treats! 🛍️

Nicknamed the “City That Never Sleeps,” Grand World is Vietnam’s version of a European wonderland, filled with lights, canals, night markets, cultural shows, and so much beauty.

And yes — we even took a romantic Venice-style Water Taxi ride through its beautiful canal 😍🚤

🏰 Grand World Phu Quoc

meta.title: Vietnam's BEST STREET FOOD in Hanoi (during Tết)
meta.description:
Oh hanoi hanoi. 

I’m in Hanoi with my family in time for Vietnamese lunar new year year, têt. 

The sound of moped engines vibrate in the air and angry grocery shoppers haggle for the best produce to feed their family. Small plastic stools are sprawled across the city and hungry patrons slurp away. I’m on a mission to find the best street food hanoi has to offer and to share what I taste smell see hear feel with you in this beautiful city, This is 100 hours of Vietnamese Street Food in Hanoi.

comments.text:
Really really nice video! I can see the dedication you put in for every shot and the effort to speak and write the vietnamese name of each dish. Thank you so much! It's just that I cant help myself correcting some details:
1:47 The "phở cá" that you mentioned is actually a very different and not a common dish, definitely not the same "bún cá" that you were having, even though "phở" and "bún" are both types of rice noodle, the soups that are paired with them usually have very different and distinctive flavour, hardly interchangeable. The vegetable is probably water crust or some similar sort as I have never seen morning glory go with this dish before. And you are absolutely right about "bún cá" being a good refreshing hangover soup, the youngsters ate it a lot during the Lunar New Year Holiday after all the repetitive heavy traditional meals. 
5:06 Here in the North, "chả giò" is usually called "nem rán" (literal translation is fried meat roll) 
6:22 I'm not quite sure about the yellow skin indicating that it's aged chicken because normally "phở" is preferably prepared with fresh chicken. And the boiled chicken skin we have here is always that yellow. 
6:53 8:02 You got the translation for "nộm thịt bò khô" quite correct but the word for "salad" here is "nộm" while "thịt bò khô" is "dried beef" or "beef jerky"
9:01 "Chè" is actually a broad term for many of different types of sweet pudding soup we have here and even though "chè khúc bạch" is the name of the shop, I believe what you had there was a different type of "chè" as the "khúc bạch" one is flavoured milk jellies that are eaten with thin lychee flavoured syrup and topped with lychee and almond slices. (Personally really love it myself) 
10:59 "Bánh tráng cuốn" (without the ending "g") is actually rolled rice paper and it should be "bánh tráng nướng" - fried rice paper that you were showing.
13:24 The higher price for public holidays is a way that businesses try to pay the employees that sacrify their days off to work, quite common here. 
14:33 The spatula is actually a single giant thin chopstick. In addition I doubt that the meat must be pork and not beef, never seen it in typical "bánh cuốn" to be honest. The cinnamon note is obvious because that type of ham is purposely made with the cinnamon flavor (the orange part). It's called "chả quế" - cinnamon ham. 
18:16 The "riêu" is actually crab paste as we would crush/pound whole small sweet-water crabs and gently boil it to get that airy crumbly cake texture.
28:14 We can let go of the other mispelling but definitely not this one because of the meaning of that word 😅 The one you want to put there is "Phở bò". I guess that you pick up the "Cơm Phở" from the vendor's sign but it just read as "rice and phở". Fun fact is that many vietnamese vendors dont really have a name and just put up name of the dishes that they are selling. 
28:24 We dont use chives for phở, that's actually spring onions
30:45 They're pickled papayas and carrots, other places might put them on the side for you to put in based on your preference. 32:00 Yes, bún chả is supposed to be served warm, perfect for the cold winter of Hanoi. Love how your mother did a ssam for you there. 
36:50 The "nem chua rán" is actually made of pork and pork skin, which explains the jelly chewy texture. The black sause tho, I think it's a mixture of soy sauce (maggi or other brand) and tamarind as we call it tamarind sauce - "sốt me"
42:40 The typical filling should be green beans. Most types of nuts except for peanuts are quite expensive ingredient in Vietnam so the most popular filling for so many  traditional cakes and sweets is bean, expecially green bean. 
Lastly, it's so cute  each time you said fish sauce in vietnamese but it should be nước "mắm" with an "m" ^^
Of course my notes are not absolute as the culture and cuisine of Vietnam are very diverse and there are a lot of variations of each dish among regions. Just an urge to share a more indigenous view. Again, thank you so much for making such a nice video introducing Vietnamese with your culinary insight, Tina. Glad your family had fun!

comments.text:
Hello Tina! Congrats on your trip to Vietnam and Hanoi! I’m honestly more proud than I should be to have you visit my city lol😭 but anyways. I do want to add some extra notes to the foods you featured here:
- I wouldn’t describe it as fish pho personally, bún cá feels very much like its own thing. 
- Regarding the place where you ate both the phở gà and the bún chả, from my experience, restaurants that covers many different types of foods usually can not match with a restaurant who specializes in that food. So the bún chả having the chả (which is the meat) being a little dry is honestly kind of expected😭
- Actually, the papaya salad you ate is actually called nộm, while the “bò khô” is actually beef jerky, and the fish sauce should be called nước mắm, with an “mmm” sound at the beginning of the second word
- The Bánh Mỳ Phố is actually a chain of bánh mỳ, and personally, independent vendors will generally always have better quality 
- I love you so much for covering bánh cuốn!! It’s always seemed very underrated to me as a dush
- I actually think you going on Lunar New Year was a disadvantage, because everyone will close their business on New Years (understandably so) so it might have hindered your food experiences a little bit
- Riêu would be more closely translated as crab butter in English, and the combination of bún riêu and bún ốc would be bún riêu ốc
- Very glad you tried out Grab, it’s just so iconic to Vietnamese transportation
- Nem chua rán is such an iconic snack, and it’s actually made by fermenting raw pork until it develops a sour smell, which is the “chua” part
Again, thank you so much for visiting our country and city, and producing a beautiful video to accompany it🩷🩷

meta.title: Exploring a Serene Mountain Temple with a Hidden Sacred Cave: Quan The Am Pagoda | Walking Tour [4K]
meta.description:
Take an immersive 4K walking tour through Quan The Am Pagoda, a peaceful Buddhist temple at the foot of the Marble Mountains in Da Nang, Vietnam. Surrounded by towering limestone cliffs and tropical greenery, this remarkable place offers a quiet escape from the busy city — along with a mysterious cave hidden deep within the mountain.

Follow our silent guide as she explores remarkable places around the world — no talking, no music, only real sounds.

Located near the famous Marble Mountains, Quan The Am Pagoda is dedicated to Quan Am, the Bodhisattva of Compassion, known in many Buddhist traditions as Avalokiteshvara. The temple is a place of worship and reflection, where traditional Vietnamese Buddhist architecture blends with the dramatic natural landscape.

As we explore the temple grounds, we'll discover peaceful courtyards, Buddhist statues, colorful architectural details, and beautiful views of the surrounding mountains. The towering rock formations provide an extraordinary backdrop, making the entire setting feel far removed from the streets of Da Nang.

But there's more to discover beyond the temple itself.

Hidden within the limestone mountain is Quan Am Cave (Động Quan Âm), a fascinating underground sanctuary where natural rock formations and Buddhist religious traditions come together. Inside, narrow passages lead deeper into the mountain, while carefully placed lighting reveals the unusual shapes and textures of the cave walls.

The atmosphere changes as we move from the open temple grounds into the enclosed spaces of the cave. The light becomes softer, the outside world feels more distant, and the mountain reveals an entirely different side of itself.

What makes this place so memorable is the contrast between its peaceful temple courtyards and the mysterious world hidden inside the rock. It's a reminder that some of the most interesting places around Da Nang are found just beyond the city's busy streets.

There is no narration and no added background music — only authentic stereo recordings of footsteps, distant voices, birds, and the natural sounds of the temple grounds and cave, captured as we experienced them.

🎧 For the best immersive experience, use headphones.

📍 Location  
Quan The Am Pagoda (Chùa Quán Thế Âm)  
Quan Am Cave (Động Quan Âm)  
Marble Mountains, Da Nang, Vietnam

meta.title: Vietnam Itinerary 10 Days Hanoi, Danang, Hoi An, Phu Quoc, Ho Chi Minh North to south Vietnam Tour
meta.description:
#vietnam #hanoi #phuquoc 
Vietnam Itinerary 10 days - 8 Cities Tour North to South of Vietnam
Hanoi - 4 Days (with Halong Bay & Ninh Binh)
Danang - 3 Days with Hoi An & Hue City
Phu Quoc Islands - 2 Days
Ho Chi Minh - 2 Days
****Official Govt Evisa Link to apply**** - https://evisa.gov.vn/
*******Direct Flight to Hanoi by Vietjet from India*****
After exchanging money at Hanoi airport, check into a hotel in Hanoi's old quarters.
******My HOTELS LIST ********- 
Click below to know about the hotels I booked through this app
Book this HANOI OLD QUARTER 5 Star hotel - https://tripadvisor.tpk.ro/PCp9sje1  
DANANG BEACH Resort stay - https://tripadvisor.tpk.ro/1HUCYrr3
PHU QUOC DUONG DONG RESORT - https://tripadvisor.tpk.ro/VvmyM59V
HO CHI MINH CITY
**********************************************************************
FOOD TIPS 
For Vietnamese Vegetarian Food, search for the Met Vietnamese chain of restaurants. They have vegetarian fried rice, many vegetarian curries, vegetarian noodles, and many more vegetarian options. 
Must-Try Drinks:
 ☕ Coconut Cream Vietnamese Coffee
 🥭 Passion Fruit Juice
 ☕ Condensed Milk Vietnamese Coffee (Hot or Iced) — rich, sweet, and creamy, an absolute must!
Day 1: Explore Hanoi Old Quarter with the famous train street tour. You arrive late morning, so explore the Old Quarter, Lakeside Temple, the French Quarter & evening nightlife at Famous Train Street with a Vietnamese lunch and an *******Indian Dinner at Indian Masala in the Old Quarter*************.
Day 2: Book a long trip to Halong Bay with lunch and evening snacks/tea. This cruise stops at 4 to 5 places with lots of activities.
Day 3 - Again, book a long day trip to Ninh Binh, which has 3 excellent stops -Hoa Lu: Explore the ancient temples of Dinh King and Le King, the historic capital of Vietnam in the 10th and 11th centuries. Bike across the countryside of Vietnam, and this biking is included in your day trip.
Trang An Grottoes (or Tam Coc): Take a scenic boat tour through a UNESCO World Heritage site, navigating through caves and lush landscapes. 
Mua Caves: Hike up approximately 500 steps to the Ngoa Long mountain viewpoint for impressive panoramic views of Ninh Binh.  Or explore the Lotus garden/pond below.
Day 4: Early morning, explore Hanoi shopping with a great body massage. Fly to Danang via Viet Jet.
If you arrive late in Danang, have dinner at Bhojan Indian restaurant near Danang beach, as our hotel is located there on the beachside. 
Protip: Vietjet gets delayed many times, so keep a margin for the next flight or keep yourself free after that so that some activities don't overlap.
Day 5: Book the Bana Hills full-day Cable ride tour with buffet lunch. An excellent theme park and the longest cable ride in the world, famous in the Guinness World Records. As our Day 4 was wasted in the flight delay, we combined Hoi An on the same day. After Bana Hills, visit Coconut village with a unique rotating basket boat ride across coconut trees in the lagoons. After that, visit Hoi An and do a Lantern boat ride. Hoi is famous as the Lantern City of Vietnam. Explore this city on foot, where you can find amazing lanterns, Vietnamese-style cafes, bars, shopping, silk, tailoring, and much more to do till late at night. Return late to Danang. Our hotel in Danag was on Danag beach.
Day 6: Explore Danang beaches and nearby beaches, and drive to Hue city, approximately 180 km from Danang. In between, you stop at many beautiful spots. Hue City is a historical city with a tomb and a Citadel.
Day 7: Early morning checkout and fly to Phu Quoc Island via Vietnam Airlines. Check into a resort-style island vibes hotel. After that, book a 4-island-hopping speedboat tour with sunset from the boat. You can also watch the sunset with a special show from Sunset Village.
Have an **Indian dinner at Ganesh Indian restaurant*** in the main Duong Dong market. 
Day 8: Visit Grand World - an Italy-style town in Phu Quoc with many colorful streets, shopping, and beaches. Fly on Day 8 to Ho Chi Minh City and check into a hotel at the city centre near Saigon Square late in the evening.
Day 9: Book a half-day trip to cu Chi tunnels to know about the American-Vietnamese War. After having lunch on tour, return and explore the walking markets of Ho Chi Minh City, which are famous for shopping.
Then explore the famous nightlife of Ho Chi Minh City at Bui Vien 
Street for a wild night out. For an *******Indian vegetarian restaurant, have food at the Gujarat Indian restaurant******** at Saiqon Square of Grand Market. 
******************************************
Markets in Ho Chi Minh City
1. Ben Tahn Market
2. Saigon Square
3. Taka underground market
4. Biu Vien walking street for cabaret and bars
Day 10: Fly from Ho Chi Minh City to Mumbai via Vietjet with no stopovers - direct flight to India. 
Read this - https://travelwithme247blog.com/vietnam-itinerary-10-days/
Instagram - https://www.instagram.com/travelwithme24x7
For inquiries mail me at yukti77@hotmail.com

meta.title: Everything You Need to Know About Hue Imperial City: Tour, History & Architecture | Vietnam Vlog #47
meta.description:
Welcome to Hue! 

We spent the day exploring the magnificent Hue Imperial City in the pouring rain... We started our journey at the Perfume River, which was absolutely full from all the rainfall, then crossed one of Hue's main bridges completely soaked but excited!

Think of this video as your complete guide to the Hue Imperial City. We take you through every corner, sharing the fascinating history, stunning architecture, and rich culture that defined this royal citadel during its golden age. From the grand courtyards to the intricate details, we cover most of what you need to know before visiting.

After our walking tour, we dried off and enjoyed a delicious Vietnamese lunch at a local spot right near the Imperial City. If you're planning to visit the Imperial City, this is your guide!

Shoutout to our editor @dvreky for helping us with this video!

#HueImperialCity #HueVietnam #VietnamHistory #ImperialCityHue #BackpackingVietnam

meta.title: Ep 3 Hội An Vietnam , Lantern City, Must visit city of Vietnam, Things to do in Hoi an - Vietnam
meta.description:
Hoi An is an ancient town located in central vietnam, known for its well-preserved architecture, vibrant lantern-lit streets and rich cultural heritage. A UNESCO World Heritage site, it features a blend of Vietnamese, Chinese, Japanese, and French influences, evident in its historic buildings, temples, and iconic Japanese Covered Bridge.

We took a flight from Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat International Airport) to Da Nang International Airport, the nearest airport to Hoi An.

District 1 (Ho chi minh city) where we were staying, It was about 8 Km to the Airport. 

This journey from Ho Chi Minh City to Da Nang we have recorded in Harish Bali Travels which will be coming on this wednesday 28th May 2025

One can also take a train from Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon Railway Station) to Da Nang Railway Station. Which will take about 17 to 20 hours.  

We started our journey from South Vietnam, this is the 3rd episode of our Vietnam series, 

In case you haven't watched the previous episodes of Vietnam, here is the link of playlist

https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLxHSKe-bOElw9DVfzDTNPDyDd3aICK4Ld 

Spices website link - https://spice2nuts.com/

Gadgets we use for Visa2explore & Harish Bali Travels.
Sony A 7 111 camera: https://amzn.to/4clE2zI
Z -90 Sony: https://amzn.to/3SO8T10
Go pro Hero 12: https://amzn.to/46GULw6
IPhone 15 Pro: https://amzn.to/3YJgr8Y

For Background Music, we use “Epidemic Sound” in our videos. You can use it from the link below.

https://www.epidemicsound.com/referral/ujnsd6

Date of Journey - 7th April 2025

As our flight got delayed until we reached Hoi An at 5pm, we had very less time to explore.

Coconut Boat Ride -  Thu Bon River this place is about 5 km from
Boat Ride Charges
2,45,000 VND
Rs 800 (INR) (Approx) for 1 hour 


After the Boat Ride we proceeded to Hoi An.

Hội Quán Phước Kiến -  This was a Assembly Hall established by the Chinese immigrants


Entry ticket - 1,20,000 VND
 Rs 400 INR (Approx)

Museum - While exploring the city we visited a museum where we saw Chinese immigrant merchant house, their warehouse.

Local Coffee Shop - Near the bank of Hoai River, I tried the coffee while looking at the boat and the surrounding.
Coffee - 49,000 VND
Rs 170 INR Approx


Lantern Street - There you will see a lot colorful lantern all around.

Japanese Bridge - Overall in hoi an you will the influence of Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese, here we saw a bridge was started in 1617 & it was completed in 1620. There is also a Japanese temple on the bridge.

Boating - We did the boating, generally the boat ride cost is around $10 to $15 which is Rs 1000 to Rs 1200 approx. The boating we did on the Hoai River which is a tributary of the Thu Bon River, flowing gently through the heart of Hoi An.

Bài Chòi - When we were crossing the bridge, we noticed the locals were playing this game, it is traditional Vietnamese folk art and game that combines music, poetry, and storytelling.

Maazi - We had dinner at indian restaurant, we ordered Dal Makhani 1,30,000 VND  in Rs 425 INR Approx and Tawa Roti - 35000 VND in Rs 125 INR Approx

After that we went to our hotel.

Hope you liked the video.

meta.title: Vietnamese Street Food Cooking Class Hoi An
meta.description:
Join me with Chef Tram Long on an unforgettable culinary journey through the vibrant street food of Vietnam in this immersive cooking class! Get ready to tantalize your taste buds with the rich flavors and aromas of traditional Vietnamese street food.

In this hands-on experience, Chef Tram will takes us on a trip to a bustling traditional market, where you'll discover the freshest ingredients and learn the art of selecting the perfect produce for our dishes. From fragrant herbs to exotic spices, immerse yourself in the sights, sounds, and scents of authentic Vietnamese cuisine.

Back in the kitchen, Chef Tram will guide us through the secrets of crafting three iconic dishes:

Banh Xeo: Experience the crispy goodness of these sizzling Vietnamese pancakes filled with savory goodness. Learn how to achieve the perfect golden-brown crisp and fill them with a delectable combination of shrimp, bean sprouts, and pork.

Spring Rolls: Master the art of rolling your own fresh spring rolls, bursting with vibrant vegetables, aromatic herbs, and succulent shrimp & pork. Discover the techniques behind achieving that signature delicate wrapper and dipping sauce that elevates every bite.

Pork Noodle Salad (Bun Thit Nuong): Dive into the refreshing flavors of this classic Vietnamese dish featuring tender grilled pork, noodles, crisp greens, and a zesty dressing. Learn how to balance the sweet, sour, salty, and spicy elements that make this salad a culinary delight.

Whether you're a novice cook or a seasoned foodie, this class offers something for everyone. Chef Tram's expertise and passion for Vietnamese cuisine will inspire you to recreate these authentic flavors in your own kitchen.

Join us for an unforgettable culinary adventure and discover the magic of Vietnamese street food! Don't forget to subscribe for more delicious recipes and culinary tips.

meta.title: Golden Bridge Vietnam: Is Ba Na Hills Worth $39? Real Costs to Know Before You Go (2026)
meta.description:
Is Ba Na Hills worth it? In about 8 minutes, here is the honest answer before you go: the record-breaking Toc Tien cable car, the Golden Bridge and its crowds, the French Village and Fantasy Park (what your ticket covers and what costs extra), the real total cost of a day trip from Da Nang, and 3 rules to get your money's worth, with real prices in US dollars on screen.

Short version: the Golden Bridge is a theme park in the clouds, not an ancient wonder. Catch the very first cable car of the day, watch the weather from September to December, and a day at Ba Na Hills turns from a tourist trap into a genuinely fun day out.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Is it worth it? (intro)
1:08 The record-breaking cable car
2:09 The Golden Bridge (and the crowds)
3:26 French Village & Fantasy Park: what's included
4:39 The real cost: ticket, transport & buffet
6:05 3 rules: weather, 3-day ticket, what to wear
7:09 Verdict: who should go (and who shouldn't)

REAL PRICES (approx., converted at 1 USD ≈ 25,500 VND)
- Cable car ticket, adult (non-Da Nang resident): about $39
- Kids 1–1.4 m and seniors 70+: about $31 · kids under 1 m: free
- Ticket + lunch buffet combo: about $50
- Alpine Coaster: about $3 per ride · Wax museum: about $4
- Grab car, central Da Nang to Ba Na Hills (25–30 km, 45–60 min): about $12–18 each way
- Rough estimate, one adult, one day: $75–90 (ticket + buffet, car both ways, a coaster ride and a drink)
- Since January 2026 the cable car ticket is valid for 3 consecutive days (unlimited rides for 72 hours). Confirm when you buy.

Prices, opening hours and ticket rules change often. Please check the official Sun World website before you book. Fog and drizzle are common from September to December; check the summit forecast the morning you go.

Not into theme parks? Son Tra Peninsula and the Marble Mountains are in our Da Nang travel guide. If this Ba Na Hills guide helped you plan your trip, like and subscribe for the full Vietnam series.

The Son Tra Peninsula in Da Nang, Vietnam is one of the most under-rated spots in the city. You can easily spend an entire day driving around and exploring. We had a coffee at Son Tra Marina before stopping by the famous Lady Buddha, the tallest buddha statue in all of Vietnam. Finally, we cooled off at a hidden beach called Ca Chuon. meta.title: What I wish I knew before Ha Giang Loop motorbike tour in Vietnam | Full Guide 🇻🇳
meta.description:
Are you here to research the Ha Giang loop tour? Then you've landed yourself on the right video. I'll walk you through everything you need to know before embarking on your upcoming adventure to Ha Giang in Vietnam. 

After this video, you'll know what the Ha Giang loop is, who I recommend you to book the tour with, how much it costs, and so much more. 

The Ha Giang loop in Vietnam is a famous motorbike route that people come to visit from all over the world, and it is for a good reason. Ha Giang offers stunning landscapes, breathtaking views, and a very genuine cultural experience. 

Let me know what other questions you have about the Ha Giang loop in the comments below!

meta.title: Lady Buddha Vietnam 🇻🇳 | Da Nang’s Most Iconic Attraction
meta.description:
Interested in exploring the Lady Buddha in Da Nang, one of the most iconic and peaceful places in Central Vietnam? 

Located on the stunning Son Tra Peninsula Vietnam alongside the pristine Linh Ung Pagoda Da Nang, this massive statue overlooks the coastline and offers some of the BEST viewpoints in Da Nang Vietnam.

If you’re wondering: Is the Lady Buddha Da Nang worth visiting? ABSOLUTELY IT IS! Come along as we cover what to do on Son Tra Peninsula with our honest Linh Ung Pagoda and Lady Buddha review for our Vietnam travel vlog.

In this video, we take you around these two must see Da Nang attractions, walk the beautiful temple grounds, and share what makes this spot a MUST-VISIT when traveling to Vietnam and planning your Da Nang itinerary must see places. From towering statues and ocean views to hidden corners of the peninsula, this is one stop you don’t want to miss.

If you're planning a trip to Vietnam, this Da Nang travel guide 2026 will help you decide if visiting the Lady Buddha is worth it as one of the top things to do in Da Nang.

📍 What you’ll see in this video:
* The famous Lady Buddha statue (67m tall!)
* Linh Ung Pagoda and surrounding temples
* Scenic views from Son Tra Peninsula
* Tips for visiting (timing, dress code, getting there)

💡 Travel Tips:
* Visit early morning or late afternoon for fewer crowds
* Dress modestly (this is an active place of worship)
* Combine with a Son Tra Peninsula drive for epic views

📌 Why visit the Lady Buddha?This is one of the most important spiritual sites in Da Nang and offers a unique mix of culture, nature, and incredible coastal scenery - all for FREE!!!

meta.title: Exploring My Son Sanctuary & Marble Mountains | Da Nang, Vietnam Travel Guide
meta.description:
Join us on an unforgettable adventure through Da Nang, Vietnam! In this travel vlog, we take you to two of the most iconic and historically significant sites in the region: My Son Sanctuary and the Marble Mountains.
First, we explore the ancient ruins of My Son Sanctuary, a UNESCO World Heritage site and a breathtaking testament to the Champa Kingdom. Walk with us through the lush valley, surrounded by mountains, as we discover the intricate tower-temples dedicated to Shiva. Learn about the rich history and spiritual significance of this incredible site.

Next, we head to the majestic Marble Mountains (Ngũ Hành Sơn). Climb the steps of Thuy Son, the largest of the five limestone peaks, and explore the hidden caves, tunnels, and stunning Buddhist pagodas carved into the rock. We'll show you the awe-inspiring Linh Ung Pagoda and the panoramic views from the mountain's summit.

Whether you're planning your own trip to Vietnam or just want to experience the beauty of these locations, this video is packed with tips, breathtaking footage, and everything you need to know.

What You'll See in this Video:
 * My Son Sanctuary tour and history
 * Visiting the UNESCO World Heritage site
 * Exploring the Marble Mountains (Ngũ Hành Sơn)
 * Discovering caves and pagodas
 * Da Nang travel guide
 * Vietnam travel tips and itinerary

meta.title: Taking the Train from Da Nang to Hue – A Day in Vietnam
meta.description:
I took the train from Da Nang to Hue for a day trip, and the train journey turned out to be one of the highlights of the day.

The trip started aboard a surprisingly beautiful train, complete with comfortable seats, incredible scenery, food, drinks and even live music. Once in Hue, I spent a couple of hours exploring the Imperial City before heading out to see a little more of the city.

As usual, the day didn't quite go according to plan. I wandered through Dong Ba Market, wasn't feeling particularly well, found a very helpful local pharmacy, walked along the river as a storm rolled in, and finished the day trying some local food near the railway station before catching the train back to Da Nang.

Not exactly the day I planned — but sometimes they're the best ones.

Thanks for watching!

🇻🇳 Travelling through Vietnam and filming it as I go — no elaborate itinerary, just figuring things out along the way.
Chapters

00:00 – Coming up
00:20 – Da Nang Railway Station
01:03 – Boarding the train to Hue
06:32  – Arriving in Hue
08:05 – Exploring the Imperial City

comments.author: @quocnguyenngoc9272
comments.text: Of the Nguyen tombs, I prefer by far the tomb of Gia Long, the founder of the Nguyen dynasty. There is a bridge now so you can go there by road. I hired a boat (as the bridge was not finished then) and took "xe ôm" to go from the river banks to the tomb complex. It is quite a way out. On the way back, I hired a Ca Huế troupe (who came to the boat) to listen to traditional music on the Perfume river, a very pleasant experience. I should point out that the Nón Lá (the conical hat) nowadays is a lot smaller than the old design. The larger hat looks much better. You can still see women with the older, larger hats in the Northern highlands. In Huế, it should be nón bài thơ.

meta.title: I TRIED A VIETNAMESE COOKING CLASS! Come cook with me in Hoi An! (+ Coconut Baskets!)
meta.description:
Cooking Class & Coconut Basket Boats 🌿🇻🇳 | A Day in Hoi An, Vietnam

Welcome to Hoi An! After the slightly traumatic motorbike ride getting here, we decided to slow things down with a day of food, culture, and a little bit of fun on the river.

✨ Vietnamese Cooking Class
We signed up for an authentic cooking class through our lovely hostel, Riverside Hoi An Dolphin Hostel. You can choose between a morning session (cooking lunch) or an afternoon session (cooking dinner). We went for the morning option to make the most of the day!

The experience began with a stroll through a local food market, where our wonderful teacher Lily introduced us to fresh herbs, fruit, and vegetables before taking us to the kitchen.

✨ Viral Coconut Basket Boats
Before cooking, we hopped into the famous coconut basket boats,the round boats you’ve probably seen all over Instagram! The ride itself was included in the price, but we paid a little extra to try the spinning version (which was so much fun). Shoutout to the guy blasting Gangnam Style while rowing, it definitely added to the vibes!

✨ What We Cooked
Back at the kitchen, we prepared a full Vietnamese feast:
🥟 Fresh spring rolls
🥗 Papaya salad
🥘 Clay pot dishes (the aubergine was divine!)
🥞 Vietnamese pancakes (complete with flambé!)

The boys went for chicken, pork, and fish options, while I stuck with my new vegetarian diet. Honestly, every dish was delicious and cooking it ourselves made it even better.

This was such a fun and memorable experience, we’d highly recommend a cooking class if you’re in Hoi An.

Hope you enjoy the vlog 💛 Don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more Vietnam adventures!

meta.title: Motorbike Journey | Hoi An to My Son Sanctuary |🇻🇳|4K|
meta.description:
#vietnam #vietnamtravel #hộian #ancientruins 

Welcome to our thrilling motorbike adventure from Hoi An, Vietnam to the awe-inspiring My Son Sanctuary! Join us as we embark on an unforgettable journey through the mesmerizing landscapes of central Vietnam, soaking in the rich culture and history along the way.
We kick-start our engines in the charming town of Hoi An, known for its vibrant streets and ancient architecture. After gearing up and getting our motorbikes ready, we hit the road, leaving the bustling city behind and immersing ourselves in the natural beauty that awaits.
As we navigate the winding roads, prepare to be captivated by the stunning scenery of the Hoi an area Vietnamese countryside. Lush rice paddies, rolling hills, and picturesque villages create a picturesque backdrop for our two-wheeled adventure. We'll take you along the lesser-known routes, allowing you to experience the authenticity of Vietnam and witness its hidden gems.
Our ultimate destination is the mesmerizing My Son Sanctuary, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that dates back to the Champa Kingdom. This ancient Hindu temple complex is nestled amidst lush greenery and holds incredible historical significance. We explore the intricately carved ruins, marvel at the architectural brilliance, and delve into the secrets of this mystical place.
.

Buckle up, rev your engines, and hit that subscribe button to join us on this incredible expedition from Hoi An to My Son Sanctuary. Get ready for a thrilling ride filled with stunning landscapes, cultural encounters, and unforgettable memories. Let's explore Vietnam together, one epic motorcycle journey at a time!

meta.title: The PERFECT Vietnam Itinerary | Travel Guide 2026 🇻🇳
meta.description:
Planning a trip to Vietnam in 2026? This is our complete, tried-and-tested Vietnam itinerary designed to help you see the highlights—from the misty mountains of Sapa to the bustling streets of Ho Chi Minh City—without burning out.

After spending a full month traveling from North to South, we’re sharing exactly where to go, which experiences are worth the hype, and how to structure your route for the best experience. We recommend starting in Hanoi and working your way down to Saigon.

In this video, we cover:
-Hanoi & Ha Long Bay: Why you should splurge on your cruise and where to stay in the Old Quarter.
-Sapa: Navigating the "infamous" sleeper buses and chasing the fog in the northern mountains.
-Hanoi Train Street: How to safely visit this bucket-list spot.
-Central Vietnam: Choosing between the beach vibes of Da Nang and the ancient charm of Hoi An.
-Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon): Hidden gems, the Cafe Apartments, and essential day trips like the Cu Chi Tunnels.

CHAPTERS
(0:00-0:49) The Perfect Vietnam Route (North to South)
(0:50-3:22) Part 1: Ha Long Bay Cruise, Overnight Bus to Sapa, Hanoi
(3:23-4:02) Part 2: Central Vietnam (Da Nang and Hoi An)
(4:03-5:16) Part 3: Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) & Day Trips: Cu Chi Tunnels & Mekong Delta
